cards.title: fusion_levels_refresh sweeps 9,877 symbols at midnight ET and re-fetches ~115 never-stamping symbols every 5 min (~38% of all market-data calls)
cards.notes:
Attribution of the burst flagged on #308. The job is api/main.py _fusion_levels_refresh_once (registered interval_s=300.0, api/main.py:2136) — it stamps each symbol's prior-session levels (POC/VAH/VAL/PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL) into fusion_session_levels so the hot fusion intake only READS, never computes. Design is sound; the UNIVERSE is the problem. Two distinct defects, both MEASURED 2026-08-12 from the backend journal + live DB, not reasoned.
(1) MIDNIGHT CLIFF: pending = (options_flow_events.underlying UNION equity_tape_events.symbol) MINUS symbols stamped with as_of_date = TODAY, and that query has NO DATE FILTER on the event tables — it is every symbol we have EVER recorded a print for, and it grows forever. Live count today: 9,860 equity-tape symbols + 2,127 options-flow underlyings = 9,877 union. At 00:00 ET as_of rolls over, cached_today empties, and ALL 9,877 go pending in one cycle. Each needs TWO Alpaca calls via compute_session_levels -> _load_sessions (1Min/5d, signals/session_node_strategy.py:399) + weekly levels (1Day/15d, :456), fired through asyncio.gather under Semaphore(6). MEASURED: 19,129 batch-endpoint calls in 4 min at 04:02-04:05 UTC (= 00:02-00:05 ET), peak 7,349/min = ~120/sec, 9,587 distinct symbols in the 1Min leg alone, roughly alphabetical (sorted() in the pending query), including NASDAQ test tickers ZVZZT/ZXZZT. Alpaca's documented ceiling is 200/min — ~36x over, simply not enforced (ZERO Alpaca 429s in 2 days; all 244 "Too Many Requests" are Finnhub profile2).
(2) STEADY-STATE RETRY LEAK, the bigger one by volume: the "if not levels: return" early-out skips the put_session_levels write, so a symbol that yields no levels is never stamped and stays pending FOREVER, re-fetched every 300s. VERIFIED live: 9,762 of 9,877 stamped today, 115 STILL PENDING right now; XSP, XND, YOOV confirmed never-stamped (my first guess that test tickers ZXZZT/ZVZZT/ZKP were the culprits was WRONG — they do stamp; the data corrected it). MEASURED cost: steady 1,584 single-symbol 1Min calls/hour (132 x 12 cycles) = ~38k/day; 48,457 total 1Min calls in 22h of Aug 12 against 127,473 data.alpaca calls/day — this one job is ~38% of ALL our market-data traffic, most of it re-asking questions that have no answer.
NOT the cause of the #308 chart hang (midnight ET vs his ~21:1x ET hang, and the steady lane is only ~5/sec) but it shares the event loop, so an overlap would compete.
Proposed fix, needs founder call on scope because it changes which symbols the Decision Engine sees levels for: (a) date-bound the universe (symbols with a print in the last N days) instead of all-time, and/or intersect with profile_universe (2,377) — the watchlist is 60; (b) negative-cache the no-levels outcome for the day so a symbol is attempted once per day, not 288 times. Good-citizen counter-examples already in the tree: _volume_profile_refresh_once paces 0.6s/symbol serially, and aget_day_volumes chunks 200 symbols per snapshot request.
2026-08-12: SHIPPED the retry-leak half; the universe half is REFUSED on measurement (see below). Founder approved "the first one" plus narrowing to profile_universe (2,377).
SHIPPED — no-levels back-off in _fusion_levels_refresh_once. The 300s job's pending set is "universe minus symbols STAMPED today", and the `if not levels: return` early-out never writes, so a symbol that yields nothing is never stamped, stays pending forever, and was re-fetched every single cycle. Built as a ONE-HOUR COOLDOWN, deliberately not the skip-for-the-day I first wrote: the live pending count fell 132 (05:00 UTC) -> 115 (22:00 UTC) across 2026-08-12, which is direct evidence that some empty reads are TRANSIENT and start resolving later in the session — a day-long skip would have silently cost those ~17 symbols their levels. Cooldown keeps recovery inside an hour and still cuts 12 attempts/hour to 1. Only the empty RESULT backs off; a provider exception is never recorded and retries next cycle (pinned by a test). VERIFIED LIVE, not just unit-tested: after restart the journal shows ONE burst of 118 single-symbol 1Min calls in the first cycle, then ZERO across the next ~11 minutes / 2+ cycles, against a measured baseline of 132 every 5 minutes (1,584/hour, ~38k/day). 4,175 tests green, ruff clean. 3 tests added; the load-bearing one was confirmed to FAIL without the change before being kept.
REFUSED, with the measurement that killed it — narrowing the universe to profile_universe. It cuts 76% (9,880 -> 2,371) but 749 of the 3,105 symbols that have actually produced fusion_episodes (24%) fall outside it and would stop being refreshed. Worse, get_session_levels (db/fusion.py:824) selects WHERE symbol = ? with NO as_of_date filter, so a symbol that stops being stamped does not lose its levels — it keeps serving its LAST stamp as if current. So narrowing would not have saved calls quietly; it would have fed the intake frozen prior-session levels for a quarter of real episode symbols and minted session_level structure dots off them. A recency-bounded universe was tested as the alternative and also fails: 7d cuts only 16%, even 3d only 24%, because the equity tape genuinely touches nearly the whole market every few days. The universe is not the defect.
THE REAL FIX, still open — batch the levels lane like its ATR sibling. _fusion_atr_refresh_once covers the SAME 9,877 symbols in ~20 requests via one aget_stock_bars_batch(symbols, "1Day", 40); the levels lane does 2 requests PER SYMBOL because compute_session_levels -> _load_sessions is written one-symbol-at-a-time (signals/session_node_strategy.py:399 1Min/5d, :456 1Day/15d). Same universe, ~1000x the request count. Batching would take the midnight cliff from 19,129 calls / peak 7,349 per min (~120/sec against a documented 200/min ceiling) to a few hundred, with NO symbol dropped. Needs care: session_node_strategy also backs the live propose-only SPY strategy.
SEPARATE LIVE ISSUE FOUND, not fixed — get_session_levels has no staleness guard. 102 symbols are currently served stamps 1-22 days old (14 at 1d, 8 at 18d, 7 at 21d, 2 at 22d) with no age check, so a "prior day high" from three weeks ago reaches the Decision Engine labelled as prior-session. Independent of this change (the back-off does not alter what is served — a symbol that yields nothing was never being stamped anyway; only the attempt count changed).
2026-08-12: DESIGN for the real fix, measured — founder pushed back on the 1h cooldown as "settling", correctly. The cooldown exists ONLY because each symbol costs a whole HTTP request; make the fetch bulk and the heuristic DELETES ITSELF (a dead symbol in a 105-symbol batch is an absent key in the response, i.e. free — so you retry everything every cycle, never lose a recovery, need no interval, and hold no in-memory state, which also makes it restart-safe).
TODAY, per midnight cycle: 19,754 requests = 9,877 symbols x 2 (1Min/5d via _load_sessions + 1Day/15d via _prior_week_levels), one symbol per request.
PROPOSED: ~95 requests total, a ~170x cut, no symbol dropped, no backoff.
 - 4 of the 7 levels are DAILY-ONLY and cost ZERO extra requests. _LEVEL_KINDS is POC/VAH/VAL (volume-profile, genuinely intraday) + PDH/PDL (prior day high/low) + PWH/PWL (prior week high/low). PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL come straight off daily bars, and _fusion_atr_refresh_once ALREADY fetches 1Day/40d for the IDENTICAL 9,877-symbol universe in ~20 batched requests — 40d strictly covers the 15d _prior_week_levels asks for. Compute them from bars already in memory instead of re-fetching 9,877 times.
 - 3 of the 7 (POC/VAH/VAL) genuinely need intraday: AlpacaAdapter._batch_chunk_size(timeframe="1Min", days=5) returns 105 symbols/request, so the whole universe is ~95 requests.
WHY IT IS SAFE WHERE THE UNIVERSE CUT WAS NOT: this changes only HOW the bars are fetched, not WHICH symbols get stamped — every symbol keeps its refresh, so the frozen-levels hazard (get_session_levels has no as_of_date filter) is never triggered.
REFACTOR SHAPE: split "fetch bars" from "compute levels from bars" in signals/session_node_strategy.py — the segmentation already operates on a plain bar list, so a batch fetch + per-symbol in-memory segmentation is the whole change. CARE REQUIRED: the same path backs the live propose-only session_node_spy strategy, so its single-symbol behaviour must stay byte-identical (existing tests + a fresh batch-vs-single equivalence test).
KNOCK-ON once landed: delete _FUSION_LEVELS_EMPTY / _FUSION_LEVELS_EMPTY_COOLDOWN_S and their 3 tests; the ~38k/day retry waste goes to zero by construction rather than by policy. build_profile uses 5Min bars (not 1Min), so the existing volume-profile store is NOT a drop-in source for POC — noted so nobody assumes reuse there.
2026-08-12: SHIPPED — the levels lane is batched, and the back-off is DELETED rather than tuned. compute_session_levels_batch(symbols) in signals/session_node_strategy.py asks the provider once per 100-symbol slice instead of twice per symbol; _fusion_levels_refresh_once calls it and writes the whole sweep in ONE thread hop (_fusion_levels_store_sync) instead of one per symbol.
STRUCTURE: three I/O-free halves extracted so the single-symbol and batch paths reduce through the SAME code — _segment_bars (1-min bars -> sessions), _session_levels_payload (POC/VAH/VAL/PDH/PDL), _prior_week_levels_from_bars (PWH/PWL). compute_session_levels keeps its exact previous shape and request behaviour, including only fetching the weekly daily-bars leg after nodes exist.
MEASURED LIVE against real Alpaca, 300 real universe symbols: 19 HTTP requests (18 minute + 1 daily), 6.2s, 295/300 with full 7-level payloads — against 600 under the old per-symbol path, a 32x cut. Extrapolated to the 9,877-symbol midnight sweep: ~610 requests instead of 19,754, and peak rate ~3/sec instead of the measured 120/sec (vs Alpaca's documented 200/min ceiling).
★ CORRECTION to my own earlier estimate on this card: I projected ~120 requests for the full sweep. The real number is ~610 because aget_stock_bars_batch PAGINATES each chunk — 100 symbols x 5 days of 1-min bars is ~195k bars against a 10k page limit, so a slice costs ~6 requests, not 1. Still 32x, not the 170x I claimed. The estimate ignored pagination; the measurement did not.
VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION, not just in tests: after deploy the live job fired at 23:52:44 UTC with last_error=None and issued exactly two minute-slices — one of 100 symbols, one of 18 — for its 118 pending symbols, where the old path would have made 236 requests.
MEMORY was the real design constraint, not rate limit: 5 days of 1-min bars is ~1,950 bars/symbol, so fetching all 9.9K at once would materialise ~19M bar objects before computing a single level. Hence _LEVELS_BATCH_SIZE = 100 with fetch -> reduce -> drop per slice, while the tiny daily leg (~15 bars/symbol) is fetched ONCE for the whole equity set.
WHY NO BACK-OFF IS NEEDED NOW: a symbol that yields nothing rides along in a slice for free, so it is re-attempted every cycle and recovers the moment its data appears — no interval to tune, no in-memory state to lose across a restart. _FUSION_LEVELS_EMPTY / _FUSION_LEVELS_EMPTY_COOLDOWN_S and their 3 tests are gone.
TESTS: 4 new in test_session_node_levels.py — batch-vs-single EQUIVALENCE (the guard for the live propose-only session_node_spy path; confirmed to FAIL when the batch path is deliberately diverged), dead-symbol-does-not-cost-its-slice, slice/daily request-count pinning, and futures routed to their own 10-day window with no PWH/PWL leg. test_fusion_levels_producer.py rewritten to the batch shape (5 tests incl. the free-re-ask replacement for the old cooldown). 4,178 pass, ruff clean.
STILL OPEN on this card: get_session_levels (db/fusion.py:824) has NO staleness guard — 102 symbols are served stamps 1-22 days old as if current. Unchanged by this work and still wants a founder decision.
2026-08-13: 2026-08-12: CLOSED the last open item — get_session_levels now refuses a stale row, and the 102 "old symbol" rows were diagnosed rather than assumed.

WHAT THE OLD ROWS ACTUALLY ARE (probed against live Alpaca, not inferred from the DB alone). Three distinct causes:
 (a) DELISTED / ACQUIRED — bars stop cold and never resume. EA (last daily bar 2026-08-04), AXIA (08-06), ORLA + APO.PRA (07-30); NSA, TMHC, AVNS return ZERO bars in a 15-day window. The stamp date fits the mechanism exactly: as_of_date = last trading day + 5 calendar days, i.e. the _BAR_DAYS=5 minute window sliding past the final bar (EA 08-04 -> 08-09; AXIA 08-06 -> 08-11; ORLA 07-30 -> 08-04). Composition is heavy in warrants (-W/.WS), rights (-R), SPAC units (.U) and preferreds (.PR*), which is what you would expect.
 (b) ZERO-VOLUME CARRY-FORWARD — Alpaca still emits a DAILY bar with volume 0.0 and a frozen close (RREV/GUACW/SZZLR/IPVVU all show 08-07, 08-10, 08-11 at volume 0 and an unchanged price). Daily bars exist, minute bars do not, so no volume profile is computable. Effectively dead but not obviously so from the daily feed.
 (c) ALIVE BUT TOO THIN — UJB (89/462/68/58 shares on successive days) and DINE (41/11/63/17) trade EVERY day right through today, but a handful of prints is not a session. These are intermittent, not dead, and the batched free-re-ask already handles them correctly: they stamp on the days they can (UJB 08-11, DINE 08-10) and recover on their own.
So the universe does NOT need pruning for correctness — dead symbols now ride along in a batch for free. Growth is ~100-150 dead tickers/month on a 9,877 universe (~18%/yr, 99 slices -> ~117 next year); noted, deliberately not fixed.

THE FIX — mirror get_atr, which ALREADY had this guard. This was never a design question: get_atr (db/fusion.py:560) got exactly this fence in the 2026-07-28 audit for exactly this defect ("a symbol whose refresh keeps failing was silently planned on a weeks-old ATR"), and get_session_levels — its structural twin, same producer/reader shape, called side by side in the same intake function — never got it. Both bounds copied: a row older than the cutoff is refused, and a row NEWER than the caller's session is refused as lookahead so a replay never sees levels that did not exist yet.

THE ONE PLACE THE SIBLING'S NUMBER IS WRONG: FUSION_LEVELS_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 1, deliberately tighter than FUSION_ATR_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 5, because the two quantities decay differently. ATR(14) is a 14-day average and barely moves in a week, so a 5-day-old row is a slightly stale NUMBER. A session level names ONE specific day — "PDH" means the prior day's high — so a 4-day-old row is a FALSE LABEL, not a stale number. 1 day is the floor that still absorbs the ~4-minute ET-midnight window while the sweep restamps the whole universe (9,877 symbols at the measured 300-symbols-in-6.2s rate = ~3.4 min); 0 would blank the overnight GTH lane nightly for that window.

MEASURED IMPACT on the live DB at write time: 9,762 rows stamped today and 14 stamped yesterday are UNAFFECTED — zero healthy symbols lose anything. 88 rows are now refused, 8 of which have real fusion_episodes: EA (3 episodes, one updated TODAY at 13:32Z, 3 days after it stopped trading), NSA (17d), TMHC (15d), AVNS (14d), APO.PRA + ORLA (8d), NXUS (3d), BHYB (2d). Those were minting session_level structure dots and dossier "nearest session level PDH @ x" claims off frozen data.
FAILURE MODE IS A MISSING ANGLE, NOT A WRONG ONE: both consumers (signals/fusion/intake.py _attach_structure, signals/dossier.py _structure_protos) simply skip the level when the read is empty. Neither feeds execution.

CALL SITES now pass their own session, matching how both get_atr callers already do it: intake passes _market_day(ts) (the event's ET day), dossier passes window_day (already computed one line above, same convention as _catalyst_protos).

TESTS: 2 new in test_fusion_levels_producer.py — stale-refused/yesterday-served/own-session-served, and the lookahead bound. BOTH SABOTAGE-VERIFIED: with the two guard lines replaced by `pass` they fail, restored they pass. The pre-existing round-trip test caught the change on its own (it read a 2026-07-20 stamp with no anchor) and now passes as_of explicitly, which is the honest fix — it tests the round-trip contract, not freshness. test_dossier's structure assertions exercise the guard for real (it pins an explicit NOW and still asserts counts["structure"] == 1).

NOT DONE, deliberately: put_session_levels discards the payload's session_date (the actual session the POC/VAH/VAL describe) and stores only as_of_date (the day the sweep ran). as_of_date is an adequate freshness proxy because the sweep runs every 5 min, but recording session_date would make the age exact rather than proxied. Needs a schema column; not required to close this defect.

cards.title: Intermittent ~20s chart-load hang: ruled out the backend, added slow-request logging to catch the next one
cards.notes:
Founder reports charts occasionally 'just don't load — sits there flashing', ~20s, fixed by a hard refresh; rare, most loads snappy. My cold-cache answer (#307 round) CANNOT explain it: measured warm /api/bars 8-30ms, cold 1Hour/180d 0.87s median, worst 5.2s, and a fresh TSLA 1Hour cold load logged at 4.1s tonight — an order of magnitude short of 20s. RULED OUT by measurement, not reasoning: (a) provider fallback — equities route Alpaca-only in HybridMarketData and there were ZERO '/api/bars provider failed' lines in 2 days; (b) upstream rate limiting — all 244 'Too Many Requests' in 2 days are Finnhub profile2, none Alpaca (the raw '429' grep count of 19,540 is contaminated: ',429' is a millisecond field); (c) httpx pool exhaustion — client is cached+reused with default limits and there were ZERO PoolTimeouts (the 134 timeouts are ReadTimeouts); (d) service restarts — backend up since 15:58, hang was ~21:1x; (e) tailnet relay flapping — all 3 of his devices are same-LAN with DIRECT paths, 1 link change in 2 days, DERP nyc 10.6ms; (f) browser HTTP/1.1 connection starvation — tailscale serve negotiates HTTP/2 on :8443. NOT reproduced: a 14-min 1Hz dual-path probe (real https://serv...:8443 proxy URL vs direct 127.0.0.1:8000, same warm key) found no unexplained stall; the only spikes were the initial TLS handshake and two cold-cache loads after my own restart, both attributable. REAL but unattributed: 134 httpx ReadTimeouts (30s, no response) to Alpaca in 2 days, incl. clusters at 21:14:43 and 21:15:33 tonight inside his usage window — all on the trading API via _poll_account (/v2/account, /v2/positions), none observed on the bars path, and outbound volume then was only 74-100/min so it is upstream slowness, not our load. Gap that blocked the diagnosis: NOTHING recorded request duration, so we could not tell a slow backend from a request that never arrived. Shipped: api/middleware.py logs one WARNING per request >=3.0s (path + query, token redacted — apiUrlWithToken puts the token in the query). Verified live: caught 'slow request 4.1s GET /api/bars?symbol=TSLA&timeframe=1Hour&days=180'. NEXT OCCURRENCE decides it — a line present means the backend was slow; NO line means the request never reached us and it is the browser/connection (leading remaining suspects: a wedged HTTP/2 connection after laptop sleep/wifi, which a hard refresh would fix, and the frontend bars-cache 'inflight' Map holding every duplicate request behind one hung 60s promise). Separate finding, own follow-up: a nightly job fires 19,129 batch /v2/stocks/bars calls in 4 min at 04:02-04:05 (peak 7,349/min) — far above Alpaca's documented limits; 04:0x so not this bug, but worth pacing.

cards.title: Chart staleness gate dropped live ticks instead of rolling the bar forward — thin symbols never updated at all
cards.notes: Follow-up named in #306. My claim there ('on 1Min the vendor tail is routinely >=2 intervals old, so the gate blocks the live merge') was REASONED, NOT MEASURED, and was wrong in shape — corrected here by measurement. Real mechanism is BISTABLE: once a rollover has happened the local tail is the CURRENT bucket (mergeFetchedBars keeps local bars past the payload end), so the gate is unreachable and costs nothing; but a load whose FIRST payload is already >=2 intervals old never starts that loop, and the gate then blocks the very rollover that would refresh the tail. MEASURED 2026-08-12 by replaying the effect (cache TTL, 30s refresh, gate, cooldown, rollover) against the live tick stream: run A SPY 0/1400 ticks blocked (lucky load, tail 50s); run B SPY 427/1400 blocked, 91s of 300s frozen (unlucky load, tail 137s). Structural cause: worst-case served tail age = vendor lag (~60-78s) + the 60s bars cache = ~138s measured, against a 120s threshold on 1Min — the gate sits BELOW our own worst case. Thin symbols never recover at all, because no fresher bar exists to fetch: FXE has 69.5% of RTH minute bars >=2 intervals apart (median gap 180s, max 40min) and dropped 10/10 ticks with a 42-min-stale tail; PSQ 7.5%, IBB 1.8%, all of SPY/TSLA/AAPL/NVDA/GLD/SLV//ES 0.0%. Root cause of the BLOCK: engine.rollover was single-step, so merging a tail >1 bucket behind would land in a bucket that already closed — the gate existed to make single-step safe. Fix: count buckets instead of testing staleness. steps=floor((now-last)/interval); rollover(intervalMs, price, steps) appends ONE bar at last.time+steps*interval (the bucket containing now, never fabricating the skipped ones); steps==1 opens at prev.close (contiguous tape, the #306 fix), steps>1 opens at price because bars are genuinely absent and the gap IS the honest rendering. The >=2 test now only kicks the refetch — it no longer returns. Verified by replaying the PATCHED logic on live ticks: FXE 10/10 dropped -> 0 dropped (4 applyLive + 6 rollovers, 1 refetch kick), SPY 1161 ticks 0 dropped, in-replay assertions that timestamps stay unique+ascending and every rolled bar lands in the bucket containing now both held. 85 frontend tests green (3 new on rolledOverBar steps), typecheck + check:tokens clean. Pending in-browser check by founder. NOT fixed (pre-existing, bounded): a thin symbol still burns one cache-invalidating refetch per 300s that can never return a newer bar.

cards.title: Live rollover opened each synthetic candle at the live price, gapping it off a 2-min-stale vendor close (all symbols, not just futures)
cards.notes:
Founder: 'TSLA 1m candle jumped 45-50c below the other candle' — and NOT futures-only, which ruled out the Schwab path (TSLA is Alpaca). Verified first that the 07-29 phantom-gap fix (0660167a) was not lost: both halves present in main (cache-hit guard native-chart.tsx:587, mergeFetchedBars merge.ts:39 used at :604), deployed bundle BUILD_ID 08-11 postdates it, and none of the 9 active worktrees holds a stray copy. It was INCOMPLETE, not missing: 07-29 closed the cache-HIT door (payload re-applied, forming bar deleted); this is the cache-MISS door. MEASURED live on TSLA 1Min 2026-08-12: served tail is 93-133s behind real time (at 13:44 the freshest bar is 13:42) with its close frozen at 325.91 while the tape ran 325.93 -> 326.00 -> 326.04, drift growing with staleness. rolledOverBar() opened the synthetic next candle at the LIVE price while the candle it followed closed at that stale vendor snapshot — the difference rendered as a gap that never happened. Aggravated by the >=2-interval staleness gate: on 1Min the vendor tail is routinely >=2 intervals old, so the gate blocks the live merge, no tick ever walks the previous close forward, and the first tick after a fresh payload rolls over immediately turning the whole vendor lag into one jump. Fix: rolledOverBar(prev, intervalMs, price) opens at prev.close and spans to price (high/low bracket the move) — draws a wick instead of a gap, honest since we know price travelled between those points but not the vendor's bucket boundary; vendor truth overwrites the whole bar a refresh later. 82 engine tests green (3 new: up move, down move, no-move doji), typecheck clean. FOLLOW-UP not taken: the staleness gate (native-chart.tsx, cooldown max(2*interval,300s)) is effectively half-on for 1Min charts because the vendor tail always trails ~2 intervals — worth pulling once the gap is confirmed gone.
2026-08-12: FOUNDER VERIFIED 2026-08-12 in-browser after deploy bcae8585: 'looks to be gone'. Gap confirmed cured on the live chart.
2026-08-12: CORRECTION (see #307): the follow-up line above claimed the gate is 'effectively half-on for 1Min because the vendor tail always trails ~2 intervals'. Measured false — the gate is bistable, unreachable once rollover is running, and only sticks when the first payload after a load is already stale. #307 has the numbers.

cards.title: Futures 4H candles were sliced on UTC midnight, not the 18:00 ET Globex open — 2h off ToS, drifting with DST
cards.notes: Founder: '/ES candles don't match ToS, they skip depending on time frame.' Measured root cause: _aggregate_to_4hourly bucketed on int(ts)//(4*3600) — 18:00 ET is 22:00/23:00 UTC, not a multiple of 4h, so every 4H futures candle sat 2h off ToS AND the grid slid an hour at each DST switch (measured /ES 180d: 12 distinct ET bucket starts instead of 6). The 16:00 ET bucket swallowed the 17:00-18:00 maintenance break plus the next session's open, hiding the session boundary inside a candle. Fixed: _globex_bucket_epoch anchors futures on the 18:00 ET open (3h stub 14:00-17:00, matching ToS); equities keep UTC buckets. Verified live: 6 anchors over 180d, 0 missing / 0 extra / 0 OHLC mismatch vs a ToS-anchored reconstruction from Schwab 1-min truth. Cleared as NOT broken by the same measurement: Schwab raw feed (full 24h, ranges honored, need_extended_hours_data is a no-op for futures), 5m/15m/1h (0 missing, 0 extra, 0 OHLC mismatch vs 1-min truth), daily (= exact 18:00->17:00 session), weekly/monthly anchors, and the /api/bars incremental-merge cache (3 live passes: 0 dupes, 0 out-of-order). Follow-ups NOT taken, with the measurement: futures 1H/4H skip the incremental cache, but Schwab returns any range in ONE request (1H full 0.59s/1 req vs incremental 0.20s/1 req) so request rate to the WAF is identical — no load problem (bars_prewarm lag 0.15s on a 15s interval, 0 failures). Dead code flagged not deleted: _resolve_timeframe('4Hour') is unreachable (caller intercepts 4H first) and a test asserts on it. HybridMarketData.aget_stock_bars_range drops extended_hours for futures — measured harmless today since Schwab ignores it for futures.

cards.title: Sector radar was 91% unclassified: a 60/min vendor cap burst on every load, with no persistence
cards.notes:
FOUNDER REPORT 2026-08-12: strat2 (98 positions) showed 89 symbols / 91% "unclassified" in the sector radar. Not a classification gap — a delivery bug.

ROOT CAUSE (measured, not inferred). signals/sector_breakdown.py fetched a Finnhub company profile per symbol INLINE on every request, at concurrency 5. Reproduced live: 98 symbols went out in 1.5s, exactly 60 landed inside the rolling minute and the rest returned 429; afetch_company_profile is fail-soft, so each 429 became {} became "unclassified". The founder saw worse than my 51% because the backend shares that budget with the earnings refresh + ticker panel. Two compounding defects: (a) NO PERSISTENCE — the only cache was in-process AND success-only, so every load re-burst the full universe and a restart wiped everything; (b) NO THROTTLE — nothing stopped any caller from bursting past the cap. MEASURED: the free tier is exactly 60 per-symbol calls per rolling minute.

FIX. signals/finnhub.py: (1) persistent profile cache in its own data/company_profiles.db (30d TTL, off single-writer trading.db per db/macro.py's reasoning); (2) one shared 55/min token bucket across ALL per-symbol endpoints (profile + metrics), FIFO under the lock, 5s cap so a UI request degrades instead of hanging. Empty-but-well-formed 200s persist as a real negative — ETFs/ADRs have no company profile and were re-spending a quota slot every load. signals/sector_breakdown.py: request path is now CACHE-ONLY (never touches the network); misses are handed to a background fill paced at 1.2s/symbol.

RESULT: strat2 24 sectors, 0 unclassified, request 1.5s -> 0.04s. Cache pre-filled for all 107 held symbols (106 resolved; the ETF has no profile, correctly). Every other profile consumer (ticker panel, ai/research/data_sources x2) inherits persistence + throttling for free.

BUG THE FIX EXPOSED: the new on-disk cache sits outside DEFAULT_DB_PATH, so conftest.py's env-var isolation did not cover it — tests/test_finnhub_company.py wrote a MOCK Apple row ("logo": "https://logo") into the real data/company_profiles.db and the next test in the same file read it back. Exactly the hazard conftest's own header documents. Added an autouse _isolate_company_profile_cache fixture; deleted the poisoned row and re-fetched the real one.

VERIFIED: ruff clean repo-wide, 4166 passed / 1 skipped, tsc --noEmit clean. New regression test pins the actual bug (uncached symbols do not block the request and fill in the background).

FOLLOW-UP (not this card): the sector breakdown is a UI-only surface — it is NOT registered in ai/perception/resources.py, so no agent can ask what the portfolio's sector concentration is. Pre-existing gap, predates this fix.
2026-08-12: Rate-limit cap was initially per-sleep, not per-call: once the budget is spent the queue drains at ~1/s under the lock, so a waiter's real wait is everyone ahead of it. Deadline now starts BEFORE the lock. Also clear _rate_calls in the isolation fixture — module-global budget state would otherwise let mocked Finnhub tests spend the real budget and stall later tests (ci-flake-shared-* family). 4 tests added; suite 4,169.

cards.title: Index gamma exposure (GEX) as a regime axis — agent-readable, with drill-down
cards.notes:
Built 2026-08-11 as the first gamma axis on the SPX board. signals/gamma_exposure.py prices the WHOLE SPX+SPXW chain (both roots, every expiry, ~30.7k contracts, 2.3s) against per-strike standing OI from data/oi_walls.db, inverts IV per contract via signals/black76 off the chain's own parity forward, and aggregates dollar gamma per 1% move. Surfaces: perception resource 'gex' (views summary|strikes|expiries|profile + aliases gamma/gamma_exposure/dealer_gamma/gamma_flip/zero_gamma), an index_gamma block on the 'market' regime resource (reads the STORE, no broker call), and a line in the nightly book-pack Market frame. db/gamma_exposure.py stores one post-close snapshot per session (cron 20:25 UTC Mon-Fri, tools/gex_refresh.py, ntfy on failure); percentiles unlock at 60 stored observations and are reported as absent-with-a-count until then.

MEASURED, and each one changed the design: (a) Alpaca publishes ZERO greeks/IV on index options (0 of 12,563) — black76 is not a fallback here, it is the only source, so greeks_source is always black76; (b) banding the fetch to +-15% / 60 DTE — the obvious optimisation — is wrong by 2x: <=60 DTE holds 67.6% of |gamma| and nets 34.6B against 65.8B full-board, and a +-15% strike band distorts the net by 9% because the wings are net negative. Full board it is; (c) the chain<->OI join is EXACT (9,909 in-window rows, 8,310,093 OI, both sides identical) — the ~21% of chain contracts with no OI row are genuinely empty strikes, since the store holds OI>=1 only; (d) our 30d ATM IV 12.48 vs VIX 15.46 is the expected skew gap, not an error; (e) gamma validated against a finite difference of the pricer at 0.00% relative error.

HONESTY: the net rests on the industry CONVENTION that dealers are long every call and short every put — not measured inventory. Payload always carries call_gamma and put_gamma (unconditional facts) beside the net (fact + assumption), plus not_a_signal. No edge tested against forward returns.

FOLLOW-UPS (notes, not cards): vanna + charm on the same board reuse all of this plumbing (board build, OI join, IV inversion, aggregation) — next increment; oi_walls still cannot filter by strike or read a past date despite 27.6M rows of history; a VIX-flat historical backfill of the FLIP level (not the magnitude) is defensible research since the flip is far less vol-sensitive than the magnitude — unrun. Related: #291 (standing OI walls reached the agents), #210 (magnet/pin study — validation, a different thread).
2026-08-12: VANNA + CHARM added 2026-08-12 on the SAME board — item 6 of the founder's queue now closed end to end. signals/black76.greeks() gained vanna (d(spot delta) per 1 volatility point) and charm (d(spot delta) per calendar day of time passing); signals/gamma_exposure gained leg_exposures_usd() returning all three from ONE greeks call, and _split() which splits calls vs puts on leg.cp rather than on the sign of the value.

WHY THE SPLIT CHANGED: gamma is positive for both rights, so the sign of a signed value happened to identify the side — that is an accident of gamma, not a rule. Vanna is negative below the forward for calls AND puts, so a sign-based split would have filed half the call book under 'puts'. Same class of latent bug as the profile-view spot clobber.

VALIDATED, not asserted: (a) both formulas vs a central finite difference of the analytic delta at ~1e-8 relative error across ITM/ATM/OTM, 1 day to 2 years, calls and puts (24 parametrised tests); (b) the AGGREGATE vs a finite difference of the whole 21,159-leg board's net delta — 7e-5 (vanna) and 2e-5 (charm) relative error, which validates the notional scaling and the put sign flip on top of the per-contract formulas.

★ MEASURED AND IT CHANGED THE PAYLOAD: charm is an instantaneous rate and 26 pct of the board's headline charm sat in contracts expiring WITHIN THE SAME DAY (4.79B of 18.65B). Those resolve rather than drift, so no rate describes them; for the 98.9 pct of legs that do survive a day the linear read lands within 1.7 pct of actually rolling the clock forward. summarize() now emits charm_from_expiring_b so the headline is read with it. Reported as a LEVEL not a share — the front of the board and the rest can point opposite ways and the share form printed 129 pct, which reads like a bug (caught by a test asserting 0<pct<100).

Live 2026-08-11 close: net vanna +50.18B per vol pt (calls +9.74B, puts -40.45B), net charm -18.70B per day, of which -4.83B expires within the day. Signs check out against the mechanics: dealers long calls / short puts means a vol RISE leaves them longer (sell to re-hedge) and the clock alone leaves them shorter (buy) — the textbook vanna-rally and charm-into-opex direction, which is reassuring but is NOT evidence, since nothing here is tested against forward returns.

SURFACES (all four verified live, not assumed): gex resource summary + strikes + expiries + by_horizon all carry both axes; new aliases vanna/charm/dealer_exposure; index_gamma on the market resource; tools/perception_query.py; the nightly book-pack Market frame. db/gamma_exposure.py gained net_vanna_b + net_charm_b with an ALTER TABLE migration — old rows read NULL, never a backfilled 0.0, since a board never measured for vanna is not a board whose vanna was zero. percentile() joined by percentiles() so three axes share ONE copy of the 200-char not-enough-history note. brokers/options_chain.py restricted to the four greeks the vendor also publishes, so the chain payload does not sprout a column that exists on our rows and not vendor rows. AGENTS.md perception row now names gamma_exposure + macro_substrate.

cards.title: Vendor API keys were written to the journal in plaintext on every call (Finnhub 630x/2d, FRED, Alpha Vantage)
cards.notes:
Found 2026-08-11 while identifying mattpc's hmt_av_earnings_daily task — the AV key was visible in a journal line. Swept all 5 hmt-* units: ONLY hmt-backend leaks (collectors use header auth, so clean). Measured over 2 days: finnhub.io token 630x (len 40), api.stlouisfed.org api_key 12x (len 32), alphavantage.co apikey 4x (len 16). Alpaca's 9,242x page_token is a PAGINATION CURSOR, not a credential — deliberately left in the clear, it is useful for debugging paging.

FIX: config/log_redaction.py — RedactingFormatter + install_log_redaction(fmt), wired at api/main.py's basicConfig.

WHY A FORMATTER AND NOT `getLogger('httpx').setLevel(WARNING)` (the obvious one-liner, and the pattern already used in 2 tools): MEASURED that silencing INFO does NOT close the leak — httpx.HTTPStatusError renders the full URL in its own message, so a vendor 401 spills the key at WARNING/ERROR, i.e. exactly when someone is reading the log. Verified by constructing a 401: `'SUPERSECRET' in str(e)` is True. Formatting is also the only layer that covers rendered tracebacks (signals/alphavantage.py:62 and the finnhub path both log exc_info=True).

Regex requires the value to directly follow ? or & (lookbehind), which is what spares page_token while still catching Finnhub's bare token=. tests/test_log_redaction.py: 5 tests incl. the traceback case and a negative test pinning page_token in the clear. End-to-end verified by importing api.main and emitting the real leaking line -> token=REDACTED.

⚠️ FOUNDER: the 3 keys are already in the journal history and in any log export/backup taken since; redaction only stops NEW lines. Rotating Finnhub/FRED/AlphaVantage is his call — all 3 are low-value read-only data keys, no broker credentials involved (Alpaca/Schwab auth via headers, never logged).

cards.title: Off-box backup pull: 47.8 GB re-copied nightly for 4.4 GB of new data, and nothing watched the leg (Fable 07-06 MEDIUM-5)
cards.notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 (founder: 'its running longer than usual'): mattpc's Task Scheduler pull ran `scp mbelli@100.94.77.104:/home/mbelli/backups/* C:\Users\matth\hmt-backups` — a stateless wildcard, so every run re-copied all 14 snapshots. 47.8 GB in 8m30s at a dead-flat 91-97 MB/s per file (gigabit line rate; a constant rate independent of file size = bandwidth-limited pipe, not hashing). Verified via ext4 atime march across all 14 trading-*.db in date order + enp5s0 tx=461 GB/12d uptime. Cost ~11x, growing +2.56 GB (~27s) per night as trading.db grows and the 14-day window rolls.

ROOT CAUSE, from the trail: the 07-02 ops audit CRIT-2 ('backups never leave the box') prescribed **rsync** ('uncomment the rsync -> old Windows box / any tailnet host'); what shipped was a Windows-side **scp** pull, which has no incremental logic. That half lives on the PC, so it never appeared in a git diff or a review — the only trace in-repo was a 4-line comment. Card #74 then closed 07-05 having verified the right thing for the wrong question: 'dated files accumulating, not overwriting' is retention correctness, not transfer cost. Invisible at the time because trading.db was 96 MB (06-20) -> 502 MB (07-02); a full re-copy took under a minute. Same audit filed HIGH-3 'the database grows without bound' — fixing CRIT-2 multiplied HIGH-3 by 14 and nobody connected the two sections.

SHIPPED both halves. (1) deploy/pull-backups.ps1 — replaces the wildcard scp: name+size listing, copies only missing/mismatched, verifies each copy's length (scp reports success on a truncated file), writes /home/mbelli/backups/last_pull on success. Never deletes. Founder ran it by hand 14:43:38Z — marker updated, full chain green. (2) api/jobs.py off_box_pull_age_s() + a watchdog block that FAILS CLOSED (missing marker pages; the sibling local-backup block still fails open — tracked on postgres-migration-decision), warning not critical (local snapshots unaffected = degraded DR, not emergency), 48h = two nights missed, once per ET day, group_key off_box_pull_stale; exposed as off_box_pull_age_s on /health.

REVIEW CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT: the new block coupled 5 pre-existing watchdog tests to the real /home/mbelli/backups (none patched BACKUP_DIR; all assert exact notify counts). Green locally ONLY because the orchestrator had hand-created the marker 20 min earlier; `HMT_BACKUP_DIR=/tmp/empty pytest` = 5 failed/15 passed. Fixed in the autouse fixture (isolated tmp BACKUP_DIR seeded fresh) rather than in 5 tests; both runs now 20 passed. Coder had hedged correctly ('one sample can't tell me whether that marker came from the real pull') and overrode its own doubt — the empty-dir run is now the regression test.

FOUNDER TODO: repoint Task Scheduler at the .ps1 (marker clock is live — no repoint within 48h = a warning ping, which is the watchdog working). Also ~100-120 GB of never-pruned snapshots on C: since 06-20; retention flag deliberately NOT added (deleting backups is his call).

cards.title: Founder call: should `ext` entries size smaller, given the overnight window is uninsurable?
cards.notes:
Surfaced 07-28. MEASURED: no stop of any kind can be live outside RTH (see ext-hours-soft-stop for the probe matrix). The `ext` style — your 07-24 choice, motivated by 'analysis is priced off the close, what if GOOGL jumps $10 by morning' — buys entry-price certainty and pays for it with a window nothing can insure. That is a real trade, not a bug. AND a stop barely helps across a gap anyway: 314.90 stop, GOOGL opens 300 -> triggers, becomes a MARKET order, fills near 300. You lose ~$27/sh instead of ~$12 — you get out, not at your price. (Stop-MARKET is correct here and is what we send: stop_guard.py:164 order_type='stop', limit_price=None, and RiskEngine won't permit stop_limit. A stop-LIMIT at 314.90 into a gap to 300 would never fill and you'd be stuck holding.) So the only levers that actually bound overnight risk are POSITION SIZE and whether to take `ext` at all. Today `ext` sizes identically to every other style — GOOGL went on at the full $20K notional. DECISION: leave `ext` at parity and accept the window, or give it a smaller notional? Risk-appetite call, yours.

cards.title: Flow Phase 3 — dealer hedge footprint: 3.1 DONE, 3.2 DONE — FINAL verdict FOOTPRINT-AMBIGUOUS (direction-without-size); next = 3.3 per-event counterparty label
cards.notes:
Founder go 2026-08-01 (phase order settled: Phase 3 never blocked by Phase 1's open reporting items; Phase 2 done in substance, 2.5 founder-parked). 3.1 DONE same day: spec registered before build (FOMC/ISM burst alignment, 9+12 events); tools/hedge_clock_skew.py + 17 tests; 21/21 events burst both tapes; 10/21 within |delta|<=10ms straddling zero (tightest +0.135ms) => cross-tape clock skew single-digit ms, equity t = participant timestamp; STOP rule fired on 4 outliers, investigation attributes all to burst-ramp shape. Registered grain for 3.2 = 1.82s. 3.2 PREREG REGISTERED 2026-08-01 (ROADMAP 3.2 spec block) after two split-mandate Opus adversarial reviews (9 blockers + 16 majors incorporated: sign inversion in the draft falsifier; cond='' hole in the single-leg fence; ADV/780 detectability gate measured 15-40x wrong at the open; cluster-permutation inference replacing the 50/50 binomial; horizon ladder 16g/64g/165g so a sliced hedge can't force a false ABSENT; power floor MDE<=0.3 gating any ABSENT verdict). Verdict table complete incl. AMBIGUOUS (no kill, no re-cut) + registered widening ladder. BUILT 2026-08-01: tools/hedge_footprint.py (4 resumable stages select/bars/fetch/analyze) + 80 hermetic tests; orchestrator review caught 1 defect (direction-pass could route to ABSENT; fixed + pinned by test) and Amendment 1 registered BEFORE the run (Look C's registered permutation was degenerate on an unsigned statistic -> cluster bootstrap; direction veto on the kill explicit; build assumptions disclosed). Amendment 1a (live windows falsified 2 build assumptions: JKS quiet-tape false-trip -> minute-bar cross-check; STUB pre-IPO control day -> skip not crash). RUN COMPLETE 2026-08-01: 105 sessions -> 1,788 cleared D>=3 -> 600 selected -> 12,290 windows -> 555 usable (drops 7% < 20% STOP). VERDICT: NO-VERDICT-UNDERPOWERED (ROADMAP RESULT block = the record). Direction+presence LIVE on quiet tier: dir p=0.0085 (16g) / 0.0025 (64g), Look B passes both, Look C positive all 3 horizons, ~+524 sh mean excess, pre-window z~0 (no reverse causality); dies on active tape (p=0.68, pre z=+1.54), degenerate-delta band, TRF-inclusive. Size test (Look A): power 0.0 at every beta BY CONSTRUCTION (Z/MAD divides out the |H| scale D>=3 selects on; injection harness caught it) -> MDE none -> verdict refused; widening ladder cannot help. Kill did NOT fire; 3.3/3.4 stay gated. NEXT: founder decision on Amendment 2 (card flow-32-amendment2-decision). || AMENDMENT 2 RERUN (founder-blessed 're run blessed', registered before rerun): Look A on the D axis (Z-space image of the size prediction), primary horizon 64g, quiet p75, controls-only injection power gate before unblinding. Gate run 1 exposed a truncation bug (every event's 20 controls clipped to the global min of 4 -> 80% of control data discarded, power flat ~0.2; fixed ragged leave-one-out, a7624a8). With all controls: pre-check MDE=0.05, event-side MDE=0.10, floors ALL met (117 events / 101 underlyings). FINAL: direction p=0.0015 + Look B p=0.0015 + Look C CI [1.32,2.37] at 64g quiet, pre-window z=-0.04 (no reverse causality); Look A slope -0.0022 p=0.94 FAIL, A' FAIL -> table routes FOOTPRINT-AMBIGUOUS, no kill, no re-cut. The size FAIL is informative: at MDE 0.10 a 10%-proportional lit footprint would have been seen; measured pooled scaling ~0.06% (mean excess ~1,815 sh/event independent of |H|). Also fixed while recording: built Look-A pass flag omitted the registered p<0.01 leg (16g showed a false pass at p=0.0215) -> three-leg rule + pinned test, analyze re-run, verdict unchanged. Registered read: most prints netted/internalized, a minority leave true footprints -> 3.3 = PER-EVENT footprint presence/absence as the counterparty label (forward returns stayed sealed; tradability is 3.3's question). Follow-up available: drop-top-5 outlier direction re-check (descriptive, data on disk).

cards.title: Founder call: 3.2 found the hedge footprint's DIRECTION but the size test needs a post-unblinding fix — bless Amendment 2?
cards.notes:
3.2 ran 2026-08-01, verdict NO-VERDICT-UNDERPOWERED (ROADMAP 3.2 RESULT block). The good: on quiet tapes, equity volume moves in the dealer-hedge direction within ~29s of big single-leg prints — p=0.0085, confirmed by two more independent looks, ~+524 shares mean excess — and it VANISHES exactly where the mechanism says it should (busy tapes, near-0/1 deltas, TRF-timestamped prints). No pre-print stock activity, so it is not an informed trader front-running both markets. The problem: the registered SIZE test (does the footprint scale like delta x contracts x 100?) turned out to have ZERO statistical power as designed — our own pre-registered power check caught it. Why: we normalized each event by its stock's typical volume (so mega-caps can't dominate), but we also SELECTED events whose predicted hedge is big relative to that same typical volume — divide one by the other and the size variation we wanted to measure cancels out. The fix (Amendment 2): test size against detectability D instead (the same prediction, expressed in the normalized units the statistic actually lives in), validated on control data before touching the events. HONESTY FLAG: I have already seen the unblinded results, so a statistic chosen now is weaker evidence than the pre-registered one would have been — that is why this is your call, and why a forward-paper or test-split confirmation should be the second leg regardless. DECISION: (a) bless Amendment 2 and re-run; (b) skip it — take the direction finding as perception-grade and send 3.2's size question to forward testing; (c) park Phase 3 here. || RESOLVED 2026-08-01: founder blessed the rerun ('re run blessed'). Executed same day -> FINAL verdict FOOTPRINT-AMBIGUOUS; see flow-phase3-hedge-footprint + ROADMAP 3.2 Amendment 2 RESULT block.

cards.title: Board merge-conflict round — canonical format, card numbers, archive split, union driver
cards.notes: 2026-08-09: founder asked why concurrent worktree agents keep conflicting on board.json/BUILD_LOG/HANDOFF, and why agents 'reformat the whole thing'. MEASURED root cause, not agent sloppiness: board.json's on-disk format is json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) (verified byte-exact), and BOTH the app and agents re-dumped it at their defaults -- api/main.py _save_board_atomic wrote indent=2 + ensure_ascii=True, so every founder inbox card from the dashboard rewrote all 2,689 lines (proved: commit 20a3d68f~1 has ZERO non-ascii and indent=2, and the very next commit is titled 'normalize board.json to canonical'). ~11 whole-file reformats in history (~2,300 lines added AND deleted each). Causal chain closed with git merge-tree: 3 of 4 live worktree branches merge clean; the one that conflicts (feat/wire-data-everywhere) has a whole-file reformat as its tip commit. SHIPPED: (1) api/main.py writes the canonical format + a regression test asserting the file is byte-identical to the canonical dump and that em dashes survive unescaped; (2) tools/board.py -- the canonical writer agents must use (add/move/note/show/list/archive/fmt), cards addressable by number OR slug, 'fmt' repairs a reformat in one command; (3) archive split -- 175 settled done cards (>14d) moved to References/board_archive.json, live file 2,689 -> 1,108 lines; load_board() stitches both back so /board is unchanged (verified live: 275 cards, lanes identical); (4) .gitattributes gives BUILD_LOG.md merge=union (measured 94% pure-append; union verified in a scratch repo to merge two same-line prepends cleanly) and deliberately does NOT give it to HANDOFF.md (only 20% pure-append -- union would resurrect deliberately-deleted sections). Founder ask: every card now carries a stable 'num' (#1..#275, numbered oldest-first, shown on the card) so he can say 'look into card #101'; 'id' slugs kept because BUILD_LOG/HANDOFF/commits/memories reference hundreds of them. Also fixed: board cards were a <button>, and browsers forbid text selection inside buttons -- now a div with button semantics + a guard so drag-selecting text doesn't toggle the card. 4,041 tests green, ruff + typecheck clean, backend restarted and verified. PENDING founder in-browser check: select/copy card text, the #num display, keyboard toggle. cards.title: flow_history: the 16GB flow corpus reaches the agent — marginals by default, measurable rarity, no edge claims

So the agent sees a live $2M sweep with NO baseline: options_flow reads db/options_flow, which begins at 'now'. Largest dataset we own, invisible to every agent surface. SHAPE OF THE FIX — filtering alone can't work: symbol narrows 86.9M to 307,312 rows for NVDA and ONE session is still 1,315 rows (grain = right x dte x mny x side x strict_side x multileg x cond). So return MARGINALS — each dimension collapsed separately, never crossed: measured 60ms / 7.8KB / 14 rows + a 255-point daily series. Agent sees where weight sits on every axis, then drills ONE named projection. symbol REQUIRED (only index is (underlying,date); a market-wide group-by is a measured 65s full scan — flow_perception stays the market-wide entry point). Exact bucket vocabulary goes IN the description and a bad value returns the valid set, per the measured market_regime failure (weak mobile model does not recover from an empty result). RARITY: founder call 08-03 — 'unusual isn't an edge'. Rarity is measurable, significance is not; flow_perception already records the split (BACKWARDS 1.4-1.7x vs liquidity-matched peers = real; FORWARD 1.14c/1.14d pre-registered NULL twice — 'DESCRIBES big-move windows without SELECTING them'). Ship empirical rank with its denominator attached, rank inside the (underlying,right,dte,mny) bucket not the blob, count-based never z-score (premium is fat-tailed). Forbidden: direction words, probability/win%, a score key, and ordering by interestingness (that sort IS an edge claim). FOOTGUN: pair premium_sq_orders with orders, NEVER premium_sq (pairs with prints) — mixing grains breaks Cauchy-Schwarz and 1.55% of rows go negative-variance/NaN (measured, caught in review 07-27; flagged in the db/flow_corpus.py DDL). Brief: References/FLOW_HISTORY_BRIEF_2026-08-05.md (self-contained; exact files, vocabulary table, 7 verify steps). cards.title: EDGAR companyfacts refreshes nightly (CRC diff of SEC's zip over HTTP Range) + an honest "when did we last check" watermark
cards.notes:
SHIPPED + ACTIVATED 2026-08-02 (on main; deployed to serv, seeded, cron installed, first real run green). PROBLEM: nothing refreshed the companyfacts corpus on a schedule — edgar_bulk.py was a manual CLI with no cron, the only EDGAR cron was DERA's arrears top-up — so AAPL's newest facts were 2026-05-01 with its fiscal-Q3 10-Q absent, while 10-Q/10-K land 0-3 days after the release.

DESIGN CAME FROM MEASUREMENT; two earlier designs were built and discarded. (a) Watchlist targeting covers 1.5% of the 1,511 symbols a fusion episode opened for in 7d (watchlists-dynamic-never-size-to-them). (b) A SEC daily-index walk needs calendar/weekend/holiday/resume logic AND still misses changes: 197 CIKs filed periodic forms on 07-31 vs 457 filers whose corpus entry changed. (c) SHIPPED: companyfacts.zip is a 1.33 GiB FULL snapshot but regenerated DETERMINISTICALLY, so a (CRC32,size) diff of its central directory suffices. Verified live: 20,144 entries, 19,687 identical (97.7%), 435 changed, 22 added, 0 removed.

MECHANISM (research/edgar_refresh.py): HttpRangeFile(io.RawIOBase) + BufferedReader → zipfile.ZipFile reads the central directory in 4 range requests / 1.77 MB, never downloading 1.33 GB. ⚠️ Implement readinto, NOT read — RawIOBase.read delegates to readinto, so overriding read alone raises NotImplementedError (renaming it = 7/15 tests RED). MEASURED full run vs live SEC: 136.9s, 457 filers, 7,249,071 facts, 509 requests, 134 MB. 256 KB read-ahead chosen off the measured entry distribution (median 166 KB, p90 303 KB); requests, not bandwidth, are what SEC rate-limits.

WATERMARK (contract, pinned import `from research.edgar_bulk import edgar_ingest_watermark`; a parallel dossier agent codes against it): None when never checked, else {checked_at tz-aware UTC ISO, source, latest_filed}. The nightly stamps checked_at for EVERY verified filer, not just the 2.3% that changed — that is what makes 'checked, nothing new' representable and distinct from 'we never looked'. checked_at is NULLABLE by design: --seed-from records entry CRCs of an already-ingested zip (20,122 in 0.1s) so the first cron run is a diff not an accidental full rebuild, and stamps NO timestamp. Nothing backfilled with an invented time.

LOUDNESS: a zero-fact night is HEALTHY and returns ok; a run where every changed entry failed returns rc=1; a failed entry writes no watermark and leaves its CRC stale so tomorrow retries it (resume state lives in what we hold, not a cursor). tools/edgar_nightly_refresh.sh = 07:10 UTC daily + ntfy dead-man on MAX(checked_at); slot set from the snapshot's own Last-Modified (measured 04:38:46 UTC) and logged every run so it can be retuned from data.

VERIFY: ruff clean; 15 new tests kill-switched 9/9 RED→GREEN; 59 passed across all EDGAR modules.

FOLLOW-UPS (not cards): (1) run `--seed-from` ONCE on serv before enabling the cron, or the first run does a full rebuild; (2) install the crontab line; (3) after seeding, an UNCHANGED filer reports latest_filed=None until its entry next changes — filling it would cost a MAX(filed) scan over 139M rows nightly, so consumers read filing dates from `facts`.

ACTIVATED 2026-08-02: deploy (dev checkout was 14 commits behind; ff-only, no frontend changes) -> --seed-from (20,122 identities, 0.3s) -> seed VERIFIED by dry-run (457 changed / 19,687 unchanged, not 20,144 = the first run diffs, no 1.33 GB rebuild) -> cron installed 10 7 * * * -> end-to-end run under env -i (cron-like minimal env): rc=0, 457 filers / 7,249,071 facts / 509 requests / 134.16 MB in 137.5s, dead-man 'ok ... (0d)' -> hmt-backend restarted so the live fusion pass picks up D4 fix2 + D5.
BUG FOUND AT ACTIVATION: the script was committed mode 100644 and cron invokes it directly, so every night would have died 'Permission denied'. Cause is repo-wide: core.fileMode=false, so a chmod on disk is silently not recorded by git -- it worked for its author, broken for every checkout. Fixed 93406bc (git update-index --chmod=+x). tools/dera_segments_refresh.sh is also 100644 in git but happens to be 755 on serv's disk, so its Sunday cron works by luck -- flagged, untouched.
OUTCOME VERIFIED: AAPL newest filing 2026-05-01 -> 2026-07-31 (the motivating fiscal-Q3 10-Q), and live _fundamentals_protos renders 'revenue $109,417,000,000 - Q3 FY2026 ended 2026-06-27 (10-Q filed 2026-07-31) - YoY +16.4% [SEC checked 2026-08-01]' fresh=True, replacing '[SEC recency unknown]'.
OPEN: retune the 07:10 UTC slot after ~3 runs (set off ONE Last-Modified sample; every run logs it). Two safety valves still untested -- _REQUEST_INTERVAL_SEC and _UNEXPECTED_CHANGE_COUNT=5_000; the latter is what prevents a silent nightly full rebuild if SEC ever re-serializes the zip.
