cards.notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-08 — the repair is fully on main. D1–D5 sit linearly in main's history (237e3d2d D1 → b0f6a148 D2 → f4d50c4c D3 → f24d395a D4 → 634b7093 D5; main is 52 commits past D5) and 50/50 tests/test_dossier.py are green on main as of today. D5's watermark import resolved and the EDGAR nightly is ACTIVE, so `fundamentals` claims render `[SEC checked <day>]`. What this card scoped OUT stays out: the remaining Evidence Bus §2.9 angle rounds (oi_walls, options_chain/IV, DERA segments, filings_events) are later one-per-round work, and EXPOSING the repaired dossier (API route / widget / ai/perception/resources.py entry) is the owed separate card — now UNBLOCKED (order was repair-then-wire) and tracked in HANDOFF's Lane-DARK section until it starts. Housekeeping: leftover worktree ~/worktrees/help_me_trade/dossier (clean, 0 ahead of main) removed; merged branches dossier-fundamentals-angle + dossier-macro-substrate deleted.

D5 SHIPPED 2026-08-02 (worktree dossier / branch dossier-fundamentals-angle). NEW `fundamentals` angle from data/research/edgar_facts.db, inserted in ANGLE_ORDER immediately before `context` — a NEW ESTIMAND (like D3's news; unlike D4). Four as-reported anchors (revenue/net income/assets/equity) from the filer's latest PERIODIC filing; tags reused from research.fundamentals.FINANCIAL_CONCEPTS; symbol->CIK from the curated `companies` table queried read-only (that module's _company_row runs _ensure_schema = creates the file). facts_db_path/fundamentals_db_path threaded through build_dossier; both `mode=ro` behind is_file() -> data-less worktree = zero claims, no stub written. ★ FRESHNESS IS THE ROUND: fresh != recent — a 90-day-old 10-Q IS the current reported state, so D4's day-count horizon is the wrong tool. fresh is DECLARED per proto and true only when the §3 ingest watermark says we checked within EDGAR_CHECK_MAX_AGE_DAYS=3 AND the corpus is not behind what that check saw; watermark None -> fresh=False AND the claim says `[SEC recency unknown — corpus never checked]`. Watermark reader lands on a parallel branch — imported defensively (ImportError -> None); `source` is free-form and never branched on. Period trap pinned: fiscal period end = max(period_end) over the REPORTED FINANCIAL rows, never over the whole filing (NVDA's Q1 FY2027 10-Q has a cover-page instant at 2026-05-15 vs the real 2026-04-26); quarter beats the same-dated YTD; 10-K takes the year. YoY only from the same filing's prior-year comparative, labelled `(derived vs …)`, never for balance-sheet instants, degrades to the level alone. direction always `none`. Live verify Fri 07-31 14:00 ET on the real 16.5GB corpus (read-only) + trading.db COPY: NVDA Q1 FY2027 rev $81.6B YoY +85.2%; MSFT FY2026 10-K rev $331.8B YoY +17.8%; AAPL Q2 FY2026 (fiscal-Q3 genuinely absent); QQQ (ETF) zero claims. Summary stays <=4000 (NVDA 3944->3938, MSFT 3874->3901, AAPL 3994->3963); cap NOT changed. 14 tests kill-switched 14 RED -> 14 GREEN; 50 dossier tests green.

D4 REVIEW FIX2 2026-08-02: prior-day FRED prints were ALL `[stale]` forever because `context` is a session angle and FRED never publishes same-ET-day mid-session (over-correction of fix1). Proto may now declare `fresh`; `_macro_protos` sets it from `MACRO_FRESH_MAX_GAP_DAYS=4` (weekend or weekend+one holiday; week-old ≠ fresh). `ts` stays ET-noon on `date_used`. Live mid-session 07-31: vol/credit/curve fresh=True (as-of 07-30), dollar fresh=False `[stale]` (as-of 07-24). Summary 3968→3944. New tests kill-switched; last-round five still RED when broken.

D4 REVIEW FIX 2026-08-02: (1) macro claim `ts` is ET-noon on `date_used` (not build-time `state_ts`) so `_is_fresh`/`[stale]` track the observation — bare YYYY-MM-DD parses as UTC midnight → prior ET day (trap measured); missing axes use empty `ts` → never fresh. (2) absent-path test now asserts the file still does not exist after build — pins `is_file()` guard (without it `regime_report` creates a stub sqlite on the read path). Kill-switch each 1 RED→1 GREEN.

D4 SHIPPED 2026-08-02 (worktree dossier / branch dossier-macro-substrate). Macro substrate ONLY into the existing `context` angle — NOT a new angle, ANGLE_ORDER untouched (unlike D3; not a new estimand). Threaded `macro_db_path: Path = DEFAULT_MACRO_DB_PATH` through `build_dossier`/`build_and_store_dossier` → `_context_protos` → `_macro_protos`. Reads `signals.macro_substrate.regime_report([window_day], db_path=macro_db_path)` (sync, store-only; NEVER refresh/backfill). Supersedes the hand-rolled `regime_macro` VIX+term-spread line (no duplicate). Four REPORT_AXES (vol/credit/curve/dollar): value + pctile + bucket + hist n + `date_used` (not window_day); missing/stale stated not dropped; direction always `none`; absent/empty macro.db → no macro claims, no raise. Did NOT consolidate the two stores. Live COPY (macro.db 13MB + trading.db+wal+shm): NVDA ea6e55… 4998 dots. Window 2026-07-31: BEFORE (no macro) summary 3912/4000 (+12 evid trunc); AFTER context×5 (index-pressure + 4 macro) 3950/4000 (+15 evid trunc); macro lines cost 345 chars; values match brief sample (VIX 17.09 pctile 47.0 n=9241 as-of 07-30; HY 2.84 pctile 16.2 n=1311; curve 0.45 pctile 36.6 n=12537; dollar 120.71 pctile 87.0 n=5154 as-of 07-24 ≠ window). Sunday 08-02: BEFORE 3657 no trunc → AFTER 3983 no trunc; dollar correctly `missing (n=5154) [as of 2026-08-02]` (07-24 is 9d > REPORT_STALE_DAYS=7). Cap unchanged at 4000. 4 new tests kill-switched 4 RED→4 GREEN; 32/32 tests/test_dossier.py; ruff clean. STOPPED — oi_walls/chain/EDGAR/filings are later rounds.

CONSUMER CONTRACT SETTLED 2026-08-02 (founder ruling): the C3 investigator builds its prompt from `claims`, NOT from `summary`. claims_json is persisted complete and uncapped; only `summary` is cut at DOSSIER_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS. A truncated claim stays real and citable, but a consumer prompting off `summary` would make it both invisible AND uncitable (the investigator cites claim_ids it can only see in the text it was given). Recorded in the signals/dossier.py module docstring. FOLLOWS: DOSSIER_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS stays 4000 for now — it is a declared law constant (a bigger budget is a NEW estimand, never an env override), and measured headroom is larger than it looks: summary 3751/4000 but the evidence tail is 1,894 chars of DELIBERATE shock absorber (D2 put evidence last precisely so overflow eats the redundant angle first), so ~2,143 chars remain before non-redundant analysis is cut. Decision: change the cap ONCE, at the end of the perception rounds, against a measured full-matrix size — not incrementally per round, which would pollute the estimand record.

D3 FOUNDER DECISION 2026-08-02: reserve 1 of 3 headline slots for min tag-breadth in the window (tie-break freshest then id); B/C = 2 freshest remaining. Measured: pure freshest-first showed NVDA 9/9/16 roundups; only 34/223 are NVDA-only. No 'company-specific' label — breadth already printed. Live: shown 9/9/1 ('$100 Invested In NVIDIA 20 Years Ago…' [2026-07-31]); +192 (195 total) reconciles. 4 reserved-slot tests kill-switched RED→GREEN.

D3 REVIEW FIX 2026-08-02: news angle mixed windows — remainder was all-time 223 (store back to 2026-05-07) labelled next to since-open 195 with no window on the total. Fixed: whole angle scoped to episode window (headlines/total/remainder = since-open pool); each headline statement carries its ET date; omit when nothing in-window. Live re-verify: 195/195 reconcile, +192 more (195 total) since episode opened 2026-07-21; summary 3733/4000 no trunc. Kill-switch window-scope + ET-date RED→GREEN.

D3 SHIPPED 2026-08-02 (worktree dossier-repair / branch dossier-news-angle). ONE angle only per Evidence Bus §2.9: `_news_protos` — exact-symbol join news_items↔news_symbols; COUNT(*) not recent_news(limit=250); primary window = now's ET day + since-open labelled aggregate; 3 freshest headlines verbatim (HTML-unescape + truncate) + counted remainder (total never deleted); direction always none; tag breadth on each headline; omit when no news. NEW estimand: news inserted in ANGLE_ORDER next to catalyst (evidence still last). Freshness = SESSION (not 30-min intraday). published_at parsed (mixed ms/Z — never lexical). Live COPY (WAL+shm) NVDA ea6e55… 4998 dots: BEFORE summary 3248/4000 no trunc; AFTER news×5 (since-open 195 + 3 headlines + +220 more (223 total)) len 3662/4000 no trunc, all analytic angles present. Remainder 223 == SELECT COUNT(*) on join. Aug 2 Sunday primary news omitted. 5 new tests kill-switched 5 RED→5 GREEN; 21/21 tests/test_dossier.py green; ruff clean. STOPPED — oi_walls/chain/EDGAR/macro/filings are later rounds, not this card.

D2 SHIPPED 2026-08-02 (same worktree). Coupled trio: (a) _evidence_protos aggregates by (component, actor_group, direction) — NVDA 4,998 dots → 21 claims, news preserved as 'news · catalyst · none · 218 dots'; (b) evidence LAST in ANGLE_ORDER; (c) intra-angle sort freshest-first (claim_id reassignment — no live dossiers to migrate). Live summary BEFORE: 61 evidence lines + trunc marker, 0 analytic. AFTER: flow3/tape3/structure2/catalyst1/context1/history1/evidence21, len 3248, no truncation. D1 cleanups folded: windows=list[str], tape window test, since-open emit/suppress boundary test, inclusive-bound comment. 16/16 tests green; D2 kill-switch 4 RED→4 GREEN. STOPPED before D3.

D1 SHIPPED 2026-08-02 (worktree dossier-repair, not on main). Reproduced on a COPY of the live DB first: NVDA ep ea6e55… born 2026-07-21, 4,998 dots (birth-day count measured 12, not the audit's 11 — blind to 4,986 = 99.76%). Pre-fix catalyst '26 trading day(s)' vs truth 18 as of 08-02. Post-fix: catalyst value=18 with '[as of 2026-08-02]'; flow primary on 07-31 = $132,347,481 / 298 bull prints [2026-07-31] (was birth-day $13.7M / 122); since-open aggregate emitted separately ($734M / 2031 bull since episode opened 2026-07-21). Aug 2 is Sunday — primary flow/tape correctly omit (0 prints; never fabricate), since-open still present. Purity contract updated: now selects the window. 3 new tests kill-switched (birth-day window → 3 RED; restore → 3 GREEN). 11/11 tests/test_dossier.py green; ruff clean. STOPPED before D2 (evidence aggregation / ANGLE_ORDER / freshest-first) and D3 (news angle) per Evidence Bus 2.9 one-component-at-a-time. Summary still 100% evidence lines — that is D2, not a D1 miss.

Found 2026-08-01/02 while auditing whether the dossier is wired to every perception avenue (founder question). PARENT: fusion-contested-wall already recorded 'signals/dossier.py (INERT, idea_dossiers table does not exist live)' as one of four dead subsystems -- that half is NOT re-litigated here. What that card could not know, because nothing had ever run the builder on real data, is that the dossier is ALSO WRONG INTERNALLY. Measured against a COPY of the live DB on the largest open episode (NVDA, 4,998 dots):

D1 STALE WINDOW (correctness, fix first). The dossier was written against the OLD symbol-DAY episode model; the model since changed to one-open-episode-per-symbol (db/fusion.py drops UNIQUE(symbol, market_day) as dead). THE FIX RESTORES CONFORMANCE, it does not invent a window: FUSION_LIFECYCLE_ROUND3_SPEC_2026-07-22 (BUILT 07-22) stamps the column verbatim -- 'market_day TEXT NOT NULL, -- now = OPENING session only, not a key'. Where the bug was authorized: FUSION_HORIZON_REDESIGN_2026-07-21 section 2.4 kills the symbol-day bucket ('the calendar day is no longer a boundary') while section 3 'What survives unchanged' lists the DOSSIER BUILDER -- the model changed underneath a module explicitly declared unaffected, and nobody re-read its four market_day filters. market_day is now only the BIRTH date, but four angles still filter on it: _flow_protos, _tape_protos, _catalyst_protos, _context_protos. NVDA's episode was born 2026-07-21 with 11 dots and has accumulated 4,998 across 12 days while still open -- those four angles read ONLY 07-21 and are blind to 4,987 dots (99.8%). Concrete wrong output: catalyst emits 'next earnings in 26 trading day(s)' when the truth as of 08-02 is 18, stated with no date qualifier.

D2 THE ANALYSIS IS TRUNCATED AWAY. _evidence_protos emits ONE claim per dot (4,998 for NVDA) and 'evidence' is FIRST in ANGLE_ORDER, while _render_summary truncates the TAIL at DOSSIER_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS=4000. So the summary the T1/T2 prompt would consume is 100% evidence lines ending in '(+4949 claims truncated)' -- all 12 analytic claims (flow x3, tape x3, structure x2, catalyst, context x2, history) are cut, including the calibration line '3 graded idea(s) for NVDA: 0 won, 3 lost'. Worse: the sort is ts ASCENDING and the cap keeps leading lines, so it would receive the ~24 OLDEST dots, every one tagged [stale]. (!) Do NOT just cap evidence: 4,766/4,998 (95.4%) are options/equity prints flow/tape already aggregate, but 218 are NEWS dots and no other angle covers news -- catalyst does earnings dates only. Capping without adding a news angle silently deletes news.

D3 SIX LIVE SURFACES NEVER REACH ANY ANGLE: news (9,873 items), oi_walls (3.5GB), options_chain + IV (443MB), EDGAR fundamentals/DERA segments, macro substrate (the context angle gets only VIX + term spread from db.regime.latest_observation, not the curve/credit spreads), filings_events (240). (!) The spec (IDEA_ENGINE_UNIFIED_DESIGN component 3) says the builder 'Wraps ai/perception get_context(scope=symbol)'. OVERRIDDEN, for two reasons. Provenance: that clause is a one-line carry-forward from archive/IDEA_LEDGER_SPEC_2026-07-15.md section 4, a doc stamped 'SUPERSEDED -- do not build from this'; no doc after it (Evidence Bus, Horizon Redesign, Rounds 3/4/5) revisits the mechanism. Operational: build_symbol_context is async and hits the network, while build_and_store_dossier is sync under asyncio.to_thread, store-only -- wrapping it makes the dossier async and puts a network call on the investigation path. Resolution: read the same STORES directly, the pattern all nine current angles already use, which delivers the spec's intent (perception coverage) without either problem. Do not make the dossier async. (Correction 08-02 after a full re-read of the doc lineage: an earlier version of this card called component 3 self-contradictory on 'zero external fetches' -- it is not, that phrase is scoped to not building per raw event. The zero-fetch property is ours to keep because it is worth keeping, not because the spec mandates it.)

DELIVERABLE: brief at tools/composer-bridge/briefs/dossier-repair.md (staged D1 -> D2 -> D3, with the live verify recipe). ROUTING: not Composer -- Decision Engine work, CLAUDE.md rule 4 maximum depth. SEQUENCING: this lands BEFORE any REASON-lane arming; reordering or un-truncating claims that are stale by 12 days just promotes stale claims. Arming itself (REASON_EMIT_ENABLED) stays the founder's flip on fusion-contested-wall. NOTE the dossier is zero-LLM and deterministic (133-240ms on the largest real episodes), so once repaired it can reach the UI + agent surfaces WITHOUT arming the expensive LLM lane -- today the deterministic honest half is trapped behind the gate that exists to control the expensive risky half.

DOC LINEAGE (verified 08-02 -- ~15 fusion/decision-engine docs exist; these three govern): (1) IDEA_ENGINE_UNIFIED_DESIGN_2026-07-16 = GOVERNING per INDEX.md, component 3 is the dossier's entire written spec; (2) FUSION_EVIDENCE_BUS_SPEC_2026-07-17 section 1b ADR explicitly hands the dossier BACK to doc 1 ('Phase C here IS Unified's investigation tiers'), so it does not override the design -- it adds section 3 Phase C sequencing (prove dossier->T1->REASON on ONE archetype, options-actor + structure co-fire, before breadth) and section 2.9 (symbol-tagged NEWS dots = the named 'first post-v1 component', entering ALONE under one-component-at-a-time -- so D3's news angle is on-roadmap, not invented); (3) FUSION_LIFECYCLE_ROUND3_SPEC_2026-07-22 = the episode model in the code today, the doc D1 must conform to. DECISION_ENGINE_FUSION_DESIGN_2026-07-13 is a different, later layer (REASON scorecard -> EV) and is NOT this build; INDEX.md carries that split. ALSO OUT OF SCOPE but owed: EXPOSING the repaired dossier (API route, widget, ai/perception/resources.py entry) per CLAUDE.md WIRE IT EVERYWHERE + Unified Addendum 2 -- separate card, and shipping surfaces for a 12-day-stale dossier would publish the bug. Order: repair, then wire.

cards.title: One capability layer for every AI surface — the queryable-resource list was hand-copied into 4 prompts and had rotted to 9 of 19
cards.notes:
Founder question 2026-07-30: "shouldn't the tools of the AI chat and the AI research and the AI managed portfolios all be synced to one layer rather than multiple configs?" Yes — and the drift was already live.

THE DEFECT. ai/perception/resources.py RESOURCES is the one registry (19 resources), but the list of what the model is TOLD exists was hand-copied into four prompts, and every copy had rotted to the same stale nine (watchlists, strategies, screener, market, news, calibration, price_alerts, proposals, reports). Never named to any agent: decision_journal, equity_tape, flow_perception, flow_report, fundamentals, index_pressure, my_trades, options_chain, options_flow, schwab_accounts. A resource the prompt never names is unreachable in practice — the model has no reason to guess the key. This is the same failure resources.py already documents as the "market_regime fails on mobile (works on web)" bug: a strong model recovers off the returned `available` list, a weak one does not. So the EDGAR statements and the macro block shipped hours earlier were invisible to chat on arrival.

CORRECTION worth recording: the first read blamed frontend/lib/chat-tools.ts. That file is the LEGACY path — CHAT_BRAIN defaults to "python" and is unset in every env, so the live web chat runs ai/chat/tools.py + web_agent.py. The TS copy was a mirror of the same stale list, not the cause.

THE FIX — derive, never copy. _QUERY_RESOURCES = ", ".join(sorted(list_resources())) in ai/chat/tools.py now feeds (a) TOOL_DEFINITIONS["query"] (the live web + mobile tool description) and (b) _TOOL_PLANNER_PROMPT (the mobile planner — the weak-model path that cannot recover from a bad guess; .replace not f-string, the prompt is full of literal JSON braces). ai/perception/context.py list_capabilities() notes now derive from its own list_resources() instead of restating nine. research/book_tools.py needed NO change — it already derives via chat_tool_specs(enabled=ANALYST_TOOLS), so all four books inherited the 19 for free; that surface was the pattern, generalised. frontend/lib/chat-tools.ts cannot import the Python registry, so it stopped enumerating and now points the model at list_capabilities — it can no longer rot (real fix = delete it, see chat-dead-ts-surface).

GUARD. tests/test_perception_resources.py::test_every_resource_is_named_to_the_agent asserts every registered resource appears in all three Python surfaces + that the planner placeholder was substituted. Proved it BITES: registering a resource after the strings are built fails with exactly that name. Registering a new resource now reaches every agent with no prompt edit at all.

VERIFIED: 109 tests green across perception/chat/books/mobile-stream, ruff clean, tsc --noEmit clean. Rendered all three strings and confirmed 19/19 names present; confirmed the books see fundamentals + options_flow through ANALYST_TOOLS.

FOLLOW-UPS (not this card): (1) ai/research/ imports brokers/signals/Finnhub directly and never touches ai.perception — deep research is still on its own data path, the biggest remaining fragment, own round. (2) tools/book_session.sh --allowedTools is still a hand-typed shell array (a 5th config). (3) Deploy pending — the live backend keeps the stale nine until serv-deploy.

CORRECTION 2026-07-30 (same day, from the chat-dead-ts-surface round): _TOOL_PLANNER_PROMPT was called "the mobile planner" here on the strength of its own comments; a caller check showed plan_tools had NO production caller and it was deleted hours later. Two live surfaces were fixed, not three. Method note: the module's own prose is not evidence that it runs — grep for callers.

DEPLOYED 2026-07-30 20:00 ET (PR #140, merge 818960b). Verified against the running backend, not the source: the served `query` tool description names all 19 registered resources (registry count 19, missing-from-live []). The live copilot had been holding 9 hand-copied strings until this restart.

cards.title: Matt + LLM is the wrong shape as a nightly pass — the co-managed book belongs in CHAT
cards.notes:
Founder 2026-07-30: "i also have no positions in matt and llm so there is no point for that to run - i also think this should be me interacting with chat - not its own nightly pass." VERIFIED before pausing: acct_fc78907f4bda (Matt + LLM, alpaca) had 0 position rows on poll runs minutes old — the nightly advisory cycle was analysing an empty book and pushing a report about it.

PAUSED NOW: BOOKS['matt'].paused=True, enforced at the _gate chokepoint in research/book_driver.py so it holds for the in-process job, a session submit and a manual run alike (run_book_cycle('matt') -> {'status':'skipped','reason':'paused'}). The book_matt job stays registered and self-skips — the skip is observable in /health rather than the job vanishing.

WHY THE SHAPE IS WRONG (the actual design point, not just the empty account): a co-managed book is a CONVERSATION — the founder asks, pushes back, asks again. A once-a-night unprompted monologue delivers a report he did not ask for, at a time he did not choose, with no way to reply. The other three books are different in kind: they are autonomous agents forward-testing their OWN decisions for calibration, which is exactly what a scheduled pass is for.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING (chat already does most of it): the chat agent already reaches positions, quotes, technicals, news and now the macro block + EDGAR statements via the perception layer. The one thing the nightly pass had that chat does not is the DETERMINISTIC CONTEXT PACK (research/books.py build_book_pack) — account, positions, open orders, journal handoff, market frame, assembled the same way every time. So the deliverable is small: a way to pull that pack into a chat turn (a slash-command / a 'brief me on my book' intent that calls build_book_pack and seeds the conversation), NOT a new agent. Decide then whether the matt book, the desk journal and its report kind are retired outright or kept as the pack builder behind the chat entry point.

Parent thread: llm-books-program (the other three books are unaffected and keep running).

cards.title: Wire the desk's data to the AGENTS — perception CLI, macro block, EDGAR statements, and the partial-bar bug that made the store lie
cards.notes:
Founder directive 2026-07-30 (now CLAUDE.md ★ WIRE IT EVERYWHERE): a data source is NOT done when the UI can see it. Measured cost of skipping the agent surface — the 07-29 panel burned 7 extra Opus sub-agents / 35M tokens / 84 min scraping stockanalysis.com for OHLC already on disk, because the headless book sessions had NO perception access at all.

1) PARTIAL-BAR BUG (the store was lying). Mid-session fetch wrote an unfinished session as the final bar and INSERT OR REPLACE froze it — nothing re-reads a date the cache already covers. AUDITED full history against Alpaca: 214,446 rows, exactly 90 wrong, clustered on 2026-07-24 (87 of 90 symbols) and 2026-07-29 (3), plus 261 rows missing for 07-27/28/29. MU stored 913.66 vs true 920.95; KLAC 208.99 vs 210.52. No split drift — the damage was precisely this bug, twice. REPAIRED 351 rows, re-verified 0 mismatches / 0 missing. Two guards: get_daily_bars clamps end to the last CLOSED session (half-day aware via last_session_close), cache_bars drops open sessions at the one chokepoint every writer passes. NOTE the clamp made the repair mandatory — a partial used to self-heal on the next day's wider fetch; clamped, it would freeze forever.

2) PERCEPTION CLI. tools/perception_query.py (context/query/capabilities) + book_session.sh --allowedTools + named in BOTH book prompts. Verified live: get_context NVDA returns 193.37 (+1.77%), SMA/RSI/ATR, POC/VAH/VAL/PDH/PDL, news, earnings — exactly what the seats were scraping.

3) MACRO BLOCK. query("market") now carries HY/IG OAS, full curve, real yield, breakevens, dollar. Built on the public regime_report so the honesty fence rides along — credit reports history_since 2021-07-29 / n=1309, making the ICE vendor truncation visible instead of passing a shallow percentile off as a 30-year one. Fail-soft: a missing macro.db cannot sink the regime read.

4) EDGAR STATEMENTS. Extended research/fundamentals.py (never a second fetcher) with companyfacts: 12 metrics, point-in-time by `filed`, new `fundamentals` perception resource. Live data exposed 3 bugs that would otherwise have shipped: alias truncation (filers switch tags mid-history — NVDA revenue stuck at FY2022), classifying periods by form (a 10-Q's TTM row filed a $58B 'quarterly' net income; now classified by DURATION), and the fiscal-year balance repeated as a Q1 comparative stranding annual equity two years back. Now ties: assets 206.8 = liabilities 49.5 + equity 157.3.

FOLLOW-UP (not its own card): confirm on the next panel run that seats actually invoke the CLI — this relies on Agent-spawned seats inheriting the session --allowedTools. Evidence says they do (the 07-29 scrapers used WebFetch/WebSearch, which are session-level) but it is unverified.
ALSO SEEN: tests/test_idea_tracker.py::test_tiebreak_stop_wins_same_bar fails on clean main (grades lost=0) — a GRADING LAW guard that is currently not guarding. Pre-existing, untouched here.

cards.title: No independent monitor for an unprotected filled position — the guard is still its own only detector
cards.notes: The stop_guard outage lasted the feature's entire life because the ONLY alarm lives downstream of the thing that failed: six `continue` statements in place_protective_stops sit ABOVE the attempt counter, and _page_unprotected fires only through that counter — so any skip means permanent, unlogged non-protection. The account filter at stop_guard.py:121, the exact line that caused the outage, is still one of those six. Round-2's breached-stop case now pages independently, but the other five paths stay silent. Deliverable: an independent check that does NOT live inside the guard — 'any book entry whose execution is filled, with no live stop| execution row, older than N minutes' → one critical page. That query already exists as list_book_entries_needing_stop; the monitor is a cron/loop consumer of it plus a dedupe. Reviewer confirmed no such monitor exists anywhere today. Also worth folding in: at _MAX_ATTEMPTS=10 × _RETRY_COOLOFF_SECONDS=300 even the working page path takes ~50 minutes to fire.  —— 2026-08-01, from the cancel-then-sell round: this card now also owns a SPECIFIC known hole, and a measured warning about the obvious fix. The hole: list_book_entries_needing_stop treats ANY non-failed stop row as proof of protection, so a 'canceled' row — from a release, a broker-side cancel, a hand cancel — removes the entry from the guard's work list permanently. The chokepoint therefore pages CRITICAL on every release failure path itself rather than relying on the guard, and that page fires IMMEDIATELY vs the guard's ~50 min. THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG — it was built, reviewed and reverted the same day. Flipping the exclusion to 'live statuses only' ({pending,submitted,partially_filled,filled}, in BOTH the SQL and stop_guard's own inverted in-loop check, which silently defeats the SQL on its own) breaks three ways, all measured by probe: (1) 'dry_run' is in neither set and is the DEFAULT execution_mode, so the guard re-submits every poll forever, uncapped because count_executions_today excludes dry_run; (2) _attempts.pop() on success plus a `if last` cooloff gate means a founder cancelling at the broker ping-pongs at poll cadence with no ceiling — 25 cancels → 25 re-placements — which can exhaust max_daily_orders=20 in ~7 min and then block a DIFFERENT position's first stop, turning churn into real unprotected shares; (3) re-protection is sized from _entry_filled_qty, not the held position, so a trimmed position asks for the entry qty, is rejected, retries 10×, pages at ~45 min and never succeeds. Also: nothing moves a proposal off status='executed', so entries with a dead stop and a closed position would accumulate in the list forever against ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 200 — measured 8 executed book buys today, ~2-3 months of headroom. The independent monitor this card asks for avoids all of it by NOT re-arming placement: it observes and pages.

cards.title: ✅ Cancel-then-sell: the chokepoint releases its own protective stop so a market exit can pass, then re-protects what the exit leaves
cards.notes: Found by the adversarial review of the stop-guard fix (07-30), then re-verified independently. trading/risk_engine.py:374-386 computes available = held − pending_sell, and pending_sell sums ALL open sell orders for the symbol with NO order-type filter. stop_guard sizes the protective stop at the FULL filled qty, so once it rests, available == 0 and EVERY later sell for that symbol is rejected at the chokepoint — including the founder's own exit and any partial trim. Reviewer ran it against a live-shaped snapshot (GOOGL 61 @ acct_alpaca_deepseek, close 332.555): exit 61 passes with no resting stop, and is REJECTED ('sell qty exceeds available position, held 61.0, pending sells 61.0') with the stop resting. ⚠️ AND THERE IS NO WAY OUT IN-APP: acancel_order exists on both adapters (brokers/alpaca.py:435, brokers/schwab.py:185) with ZERO production callers — grepped. Books are buy-only with source book_*, so _strategy_id_from_source returns None and the exit engine never manages them either. Net: the founder must use Alpaca's own UI to free his own position — wrong failure mode for a cockpit whose thesis is propose → tap approve. BECOMES REACHABLE ON THE NEXT BACKEND RESTART, since that is when the guard first arms. Needs a design decision, not a one-liner: either a cancel-stop path behind the chokepoint (cancel-then-sell, with the stop re-placed if the sell is rejected), or exclude protective stops from pending_sell and let the broker arbitrate — the second is simpler but can oversell if the stop triggers mid-flight. Recommend the first.  —— SHIPPED 2026-08-01, option 1 as recommended. ExecutionService.submit recognises the one rejection a release can fix (RiskCheckResult.blocked_by_pending_sells, set ONLY when open sells consumed the position — a plain oversell of shares that aren't there stays a plain rejection), cancels OUR OWN stops, re-polls, revalidates, places the exit, re-polls again, and re-stops the residual at the same trigger. MARKET EQUITY ONLY: a resting limit can sit unfilled for a session (→ oco-exit-pair), and an option intent carries the bare UNDERLYING in intent.symbol so an unguarded lookup would cancel the equity stop and re-stop a share count computed from a contract count. Scoping is the safety property: list_open_protective_stops matches order_type='stop' rows WITH a broker_order_id, so a stop the founder set by hand at the broker has no row and is never touched. Every failure path pages CRITICAL immediately — that page, not the stop guard, is the safety net (see the limitation on unprotected-position-monitor). 4 Opus reviewers over 2 rounds, each finding reproduced with a probe: re-stop sized from the released stop's own qty could commit 50 sells against 30 held after a founder trim (now capped by post-exit observed uncommitted shares, counting the exit exactly once whether it rests or fills); a concurrent submit could walk the cancel→place window for two 50-share sells against 50 held (the release path now holds the submit lock to a placed exit); the post-cancel snapshot hid the exit (re-polled after the place); a mid-sweep exception lost already-cancelled stops (caller-owned accumulator + write-ahead row status, reverted only if the broker refuses); a lost place RESPONSE (read timeout → AlpacaError, indistinguishable from a rejection) restored a stop on top of a live sell (now checks aget_order_by_client_id first, unknown ⇒ page not restore); an exception after a live place marked the row 'error', which reconcile never revisits, losing the fill (post-place work is now best-effort and never downgrades a submitted row); and the residual re-stop had no already-through-the-market gate (that check lives in stop_guard, not RiskEngine). Verified live: AMZN 50 @ acct_alpaca_fable (stop 233.00) and GOOGL 61 @ acct_alpaca_deepseek (stop 314.90) were both locked at available 0; the query resolves both.

cards.title: Ext-hours soft stop — the ONLY protection possible outside RTH; extends existing exit_engine, does not replace the broker stop
cards.notes: Founder ask 07-28: 'does it make sense to build ourselves a watcher? llm submits the stop to it - once the buy fills it's alerted - if price hits stop - it sends an order to close?' Answer: yes, and nearly every piece already exists and is already running. ★ MEASURED 07-28 by live paper probe (acct_fc78907f4bda) — the constraint that forces this: limit (GTC, RTH) + bracket/oto -> ACCEPTED, child legs 'held', arm on fill | ext (GTC limit + extended_hours) + bracket/oto -> 403 'do not support extended hours trading' | moo (tif=opg) + bracket/oto -> 422 'support only day or gtc time_in_force' | stop / stop_limit + extended_hours=true -> 422 'not eligible for extended hours trading'. So NO stop of any kind can be live outside RTH — native brackets are a red herring, and a perfect bracket implementation would have left GOOGL exactly as exposed. Child legs inherit the PARENT's tif (day parent -> child dies at that session's close; gtc parent -> ~90d), so the 07-24 'day-bracket children die at the close' note is real but avoidable with a GTC parent. ★ THE DATA GATE PASSES (expected to be the blocker; it isn't): the broker snapshot's current_price is LIVE overnight — GOOGL 21:00 ET 326.34 / 23:00 324.60 / 01:00 324.33 / 03:00 325.25, tracking Alpaca's overnight venue (feed=boats) tick for tick. The poll loop already runs 24/7 (~350 polls/hr overnight, measured), so we are ALREADY pulling a live overnight mark for every held position. SIP covers 04:00-19:59 ET, boats covers 20:00-03:59 ET; together 24h continuous. Also: overnight liquidity is NOT the trap first claimed — GOOGL did 8-17k sh/hr overnight, so 61 shares is nothing. That becomes a per-name liquidity GATE, not a reason to skip. ALREADY BUILT: 24/7 poll loop; live overnight price; managed_positions (stop/target/high-water state); exit_engine (evaluates vs snapshot, closes via ExecutionService.submit -> the chokepoint); and the stop price itself, already sitting unused in the proposal payload — no new 'LLM submits the stop' interface is needed. ACTUAL WORK: (a) book entries never get a managed_positions row (only auto_entry does); (b) exit_engine._strategy_kind() dispatches earnings/dip/vix_spike, a book position falls through to unknown_kind -> skip (the books spec deliberately set 'scan/exit-engine skip book'); (c) the exit order MUST be a marketable ext-hours LIMIT — market orders are rejected outside RTH, so the founder's 'sends a mkt order' works in RTH only; (d) STAND-DOWN so the soft stop and the broker stop cannot both fire — double-sell = short 61; RiskEngine's sell_position check should backstop but the design must be explicit, not lean on it. SHAPE: broker GTC stop stays PRIMARY (survives our backend dying, no data dependency, no latency); the soft stop covers ONLY the ~17.5h/day the broker stop legally cannot, and cedes during RTH. Needs a confirmation rule (N consecutive polls below, or min size behind the print) so one wide overnight quote can't stop us out on noise — PRE-REGISTERED, not improvised. Auto-execute = Rung 3: ships DISABLED, founder arms, always through ExecutionService.submit(), never a direct broker call. ⏳ OPEN QUESTION TO PRE-REGISTER BEFORE ARMING: is acting at 03:00 actually better than waiting for the open? Hard news gap, yes. Ordinary overnight chop, we'd be selling thin into a move that reverts by 09:30. We now have the data (boats + our own snapshots) to measure historical overnight breaches and revert-by-open rates rather than guess. SEQUENCING: behind stop-guard-never-fires (one line, covers RTH, broker-side = categorically stronger). (a) is shared plumbing with that card and unlocks book positions for every subsystem that reads open positions.

cards.title: Book-account activity invisible in cockpit: alpaca ledger sync is single-account + toolbar DAY tile ignores the selector
cards.notes: Found 07-28 alongside stop-guard-never-fires. Two independent read-side gaps, one symptom: the founder's GOOGL fill showed nowhere in the dashboard. (1) BACKEND — trading/sync.py sync_alpaca() is hardwired to ONE account: get_or_create_broker_account('alpaca') + the default get_broker('alpaca') adapter. The five sub-accounts (deepseek/fable/open/strat1/strat2) each have their own connection and are NEVER ledger-synced. trade_accounts.last_synced_at is NULL for all five; trade_events has zero rows for any of them; last alpaca_api event is 2026-06-23. So /api/performance/dashboard?account_id=acct_alpaca_deepseek returns all zeros and day-pnl returns has_activity:false — true for EVERY trade the books have ever made, not just this one. (2) FRONTEND — useDayPnl() (frontend/lib/workspace/use-day-pnl.ts:8) calls fetchPortfolioHistory('1D') with no account_id, so api/main.py:3623 falls through to the DEFAULT broker account. The toolbar DAY tile therefore shows Matt+LLM regardless of which paper account is selected. useLedgerDayPnl is wired for real/Schwab scope only. NOT broken: /api/snapshot itself carries the position correctly (deepseek pv 100,419.09, GOOGL 61 @ 327, unrealized +417.55) — VALUE/CASH/UNREAL render fine when Deep Seek is selected.

cards.title: ⚠️ SAFETY: stop_guard has NEVER placed a stop — account_id dropped by _row_to_proposal, every candidate skipped silently
cards.notes: Found 07-28 investigating an unprotected fill. DeepSeek book GOOGL exec_7958562468e9, 61 @ 327.00 filled 07-27 18:25 ET; stop should be 314.90 (in the proposal payload + the book's journal: 'stop $314.90 GTC. Falsifier: close below $315'). Still naked as of 07-30 00:19 (+$592.92 unrealized, ZERO open orders at broker). ROOT CAUSE: trading/stop_guard.py:118 filters row.get('account_id') != account_id, and place_protective_stops is ONLY ever called with a non-None account_id (api/main.py:359, inside _poll_account). But db/paper_orders.py _row_to_proposal() builds its dict from a hardcoded key list + _NEW_COLUMNS, which OMITS account_id though the column exists and is populated -> lookup is always None, never matches, every candidate skipped every poll. Verified by running list_book_entries_needing_stop() against the live DB: 3 rows, all 'acct None'. Zero rows have ever existed with proposal_id LIKE 'stop|%' — the guard has placed nothing since it shipped (9f72e0e). FAILS SILENTLY: the continue sits ABOVE the attempt counter, so the _MAX_ATTEMPTS 'UNPROTECTED position' critical page can never fire either. GOOGL 07-27 was the FIRST book entry ever to fill (4 prior expired/still resting), so the guard's first live test was its first failure. ⚠️ WHY EXISTING TESTS MISS IT: tests/test_book_execution_round.py calls place_protective_stops('alpaca', db_path=db) with NO account_id — the filter is never exercised. Fix needs an account-scoped regression test. ⚠️⚠️ MEASURED 07-28, and it makes the timing load-bearing: Alpaca REJECTS a protective stop whose trigger is already breached — 422 'stop price must be less than current price'. So the guard MUST place the stop immediately on fill while price is still above it. Place it at 18:25 with GOOGL at 327 -> accepted, rests, live at 09:30. Try at 09:31 after a gap to 300 -> 422, no stop at all, and the guard burns 10 retries then pages. The recovery path fails in exactly the scenario it exists for; 're-place it each morning' is NOT a workaround. Fix is ~one line + tests. ⚠️ A SECOND book entry is resting right now (paper_9fa4e9a31332, Fable, GOOGL 54 @ 328, submitted 07-29, expires 07-30 19:59) — it will repeat this on fill. ✅ FIX WRITTEN 07-30 (branch fix/stop-guard-account-scope, off main): db/paper_orders.py _row_to_proposal now copies account_id explicitly, with a comment naming the trap — the field migrates via _add_column_if_missing OUTSIDE _NEW_COLUMNS, so the loop that carries the other late columns never carried it. VERIFIED THE FIX IS SUFFICIENT, not just necessary: the id formats on both sides of the filter match exactly (trade_accounts.id = 'acct_alpaca_deepseek' = paper_order_proposals.account_id), so nothing else blocks the compare — checked against the live DB because [[workspace-ledger-account-id-mismatch]] made that the obvious way for a one-line fix to look right and still do nothing. TESTS: two added to tests/test_book_execution_round.py — test_stop_guard_scopes_to_the_owning_account (the production path: asserts the owning account IS protected AND a sibling account's entry is skipped rather than dropped, so it stays protectable on its own poll) and test_proposal_rows_carry_account_id (pins the field at the db seam where the bug actually lived). Both PROVEN to catch it: reverted the one-line fix and confirmed both fail, restored and confirmed both pass. _seed_book_entry now takes account_id. Full suite 3015 passed (pytest's own exit code, not a piped tail), ruff clean. ⚠️ SIBLING VICTIM FOUND, same dropped field, fixed by the same line: signals/push.py _proposal_account_label reads proposal.get('account_id') off a create_pending_proposal row, so the phone approval card's account label has ALWAYS been blank — that label was added 07-23 on the founder's own ask ('the approval card didn't say which book was trading') and never once worked. Blast radius checked: no production code splats a proposal dict, so the added key is purely additive. ⏳ NOT YET VERIFIED LIVE — staying in_progress until the poll loop is observed placing a real stop| execution row (zero have ever existed). On the next poll of acct_alpaca_deepseek the guard should place GTC stop sell 61 GOOGL @ 314.90; that order is only ACCEPTABLE while spot stays above 314.90, so if GOOGL trades below it first the placement 422s and the position needs a manual flatten decision instead. CLAUDE.md wants TWO parallel Opus reviewers on any trading/ change before commit — not run here (agents were out of scope for this session); the founder should decide whether to run them before merge. ✅ MERGED TO MAIN 07-30: PR #138, CI green, merge commit 054b5f8; dev tree fast-forwarded so the checkout carries the fix. Verified the merge could not disturb the 10 running equity-bar backfill shards — the diff never touches tools/equity_bars_5min_backfill.py, and a running interpreter holds its source in memory anyway; all 10 confirmed still running after the pull. ⚠️ THE GUARD IS STILL DISARMED IN THE LIVE PROCESS: the backend is a bare uvicorn (pid 2458, no --reload) that loaded the pre-fix module at start, so it arms only on the next restart — deliberately NOT restarted here (founder: paper only, not urgent, he'll set stops by hand). First restart should place GTC stop sell 61 GOOGL @ 314.90 on the next acct_alpaca_deepseek poll; that is the observation this card is still open for. ✅ ROUND 2 (post-review follow-ups, branch fix/stop-guard-followups): (a) BUG CLASS REMOVED — account_id folded into _NEW_COLUMNS and both the bespoke copy in _row_to_proposal and the separate _add_column_if_missing call deleted, so the next late-added column cannot reproduce this; the ALTER loop already swallows duplicate-column. (b) MISSED INSTANCE FIXED — list_pending_proposals rebuilt a SLIM dict that dropped account_id again, so api/ai_routes.py:219 still returned account_label:null for every pending proposal; round 1 never reached it. (c) BREACHED-STOP REFUSAL — place_protective_stops now takes the poll's already-fetched positions (no extra broker call) and REFUSES to submit a stop at/below the market, paging critical once instead; submitting it would market-sell the whole position on acceptance. Real class in our data: paper_419b12c4be9b states stop 880 vs MU ~739 close. Backward compatible — no positions means unchanged behavior. Retry budget deliberately NOT consumed (retrying cannot un-breach a stop), tracked in a separate one-shot _breach_paged set. ★ SELF-HEALS: _breach_paged gates the PAGE only, never the placement, so a dip-then-rally gets its stop on a later poll — orchestrator-added test_stop_guard_protects_once_a_breach_recovers covers exactly that, the one case the delegated round missed. Every new test mutation-proven to fail without its logic. Full suite 3,020 passed (pytest's own exit code), ruff clean. ⚠️ STILL arms only on the next backend restart (live uvicorn holds pre-fix code), and still never observed placing a real stop — card stays in_progress for that. ✅✅ VERIFIED LIVE 07-30 02:57:04Z — THE GUARD HAS FIRED, for the first time in its life. The 02:56:40 reboot restarted the backend onto the fixed code and 24 SECONDS LATER the poll placed exec_b6551e0b5b5b = stop|paper_b948c4df16ac: GTC stop sell 61 GOOGL @ 314.90, acct_alpaca_deepseek, broker order 1a380c57-80b0-431a-8607-5052482b8b5c, status submitted, every RiskEngine check pass ('sell_position: pass: closing 61 of 61.0 long'). Before it, proposal_id LIKE 'stop|%' had zero rows for the feature's entire life. That row is the end-to-end production proof this card was held open for, so → done. The GOOGL 61 that sat naked from 07-27 is now protected. ⚠️ AND the predicted side effect went live with it: pending_sell now equals the full 61, so available == 0 and any further GOOGL sell in that account is rejected at the chokepoint with no in-app cancel path — tracked on resting-stop-locks-the-position, which is no longer hypothetical. Useful precedent found in the placed order's own risk row: 'open_orders_cap: exempt: protective stop' and 'daily_orders: exempt: protective stop' already exist, so RiskEngine HAS a protective-stop exemption concept — extending it to pending_sell has in-codebase precedent and is the cheaper of that card's two options.

cards.title: Settings writes are last-writer-wins from per-process caches -- a stale cache silently deletes other writers' keys
cards.notes: Found 2026-07-27, live data loss: options_flow.provider=databento (armed ~13:15) vanished from settings.json at 14:54 -- the backend's _settings_cache was built before the arming, and a phone watchlist edit (PUT through the backend) called save_settings(current) from that stale cache, rewriting the file WITHOUT the key. The collector then restarted onto the Alpaca lane silently. Mechanism: config/settings.py caches effective settings per process; save_settings writes the whole cached dict; any process whose cache predates another writer's key drops that key on its next save. reload_settings() exists but nothing calls it on cross-process writes. FIX SKETCH: save paths must read-modify-write against the FILE under the lock (re-read settings.json, deep-merge the delta, write), not dump the process cache; alternatively a version/mtime check that reloads before save. Recovered same day: key re-armed + backend restarted so its cache carries it. ⚠️ Until fixed, ANY settings edit from a process started before an out-of-band settings change can repeat this.

cards.title: Alpaca quote stream flapping: keepalive ping timeout every ~60-90s during RTH since 07-23
cards.notes:
Spotted by the Mac agent in serv logs 2026-07-27; measured here. hmt-backend brokers.market_stream: 'sent 1011 keepalive ping timeout; no close frame received' -> reconnect in 2s, self-heals every time. Counts/day: 3-12 background through 07-22, then 45 (07-23), 48 (07-24), ~1 on the weekend, 40+ today -- trading days only, RTH only, today starting 13:30:28 UTC (the open, to the second). RULED OUT: our event-loop stalls (max 7.0s recovered vs ping_timeout=20s; flap timestamps do not line up with stall timestamps). Direction of blame: WE send the ping, Alpaca fails to answer for 20s and sends no close frame -- upstream congestion or a per-connection/account interaction. Onset follows the 07-22 deploys (Alpaca news WS v1beta1/news went live that day = a second standing WS to Alpaca infra from the same account/process). No 'market stream cap' warnings. Impact per flap: 2s gap + resubscribe + baseline reseed on the watchlist quote lane. NEXT ROUND: correlate flap times against news-WS activity; try disabling the news WS for one session as the A/B; log subscribed-symbol count at connect; consider ping_timeout bump only if evidence supports tolerance over cause.

[2026-07-27 DIAGNOSIS REVISED] Upstream-leaning read was likely WRONG. Stalls, quote flaps, and news-stream flaps all exploded together on 07-23 (stalls 14->271/day). The news flap mechanism is proven and fixed: a 'database is locked' from _store_items propagated into the outer except and TORE DOWN a healthy socket (signals/news_stream.py; now caught + dropped, REST backfill covers). The quote-stream keepalive flap is now presumed collateral of the same loop congestion (at 271-479 stalls/day, cumulative reader starvation inside a 20s pong window is plausible). VERIFY: after the loop fixes deploy, count flaps at tomorrow's open; if they persist at ~40/day with a healthy loop, reopen the upstream/news-WS-A-B theory.

[2026-07-27 COLLECTOR ROUND] Backend post-deploy A/B: 1 stall / 0 flaps in the first 30 min (vs 40 flaps in the prior 2h). But hmt-flow-collector lock errors did NOT collapse (121 in 30 min post-deploy) -- its own disease: db/options_flow.insert_event ran init_db per INSERT, and init takes write txns (ingest_seq backfill + bus upsert + DDL), so the two writer lanes serialized on init and the losing sweep cycle DROPPED its events ('cycle failed'). Bonus fixes in the same commit: dbn_stream.acked_market_wide was stale-False from the pre-widening parent-symbol era -- every whole-market event mis-stamped coverage=watchlist_capped; now True + runner stamps coverage=market_wide on burst/cluster/sweep events (Alpaca lane keeps the default). Probe after the four init guards: lock-wait p50 729ms->8ms, failures 5/30->0/20, but p90 still ~7s. py-spy ptrace-blocked -> built a slow-write-txn logger into db/base.connect (PR #119, HMT_SLOW_TXN_MS=1500 default) which named the holder in 4 minutes: fusion _rescore held the lock 3-8s x12 because its episode_id UPDATE + per-collapsed-dot dot_id UPDATEs each FULL-SCANNED 591k unindexed fusion_dispositions rows inside one txn. [2026-07-28 AFTER-CLOSE A/B] 07-27 full-day counts mix pre/post-fix hours: flaps 52/day, collector locked 735/day -- but split at the FINAL fixed deploy (17:36:57Z): the day's LAST locked error was 17:36:41 (16s before it came up), then ZERO for the remaining 2.4 RTH hours; all 506 dropped cycles were pre-fix. cards.title: Event-loop stall class at the open (2-7s, 271-479/day since 07-23) — three sync-on-loop offenders fixed
cards.notes:
Found 2026-07-27 while chasing the Alpaca stream flap (NOT its cause -- flaps uncorrelated). loop_probe: ~27 stalls of 2-7s during 13:00-15:00 UTC, market hours. MainThread stack caught in the act: api/main.py:542 _signal_scan_loop -> run_signal_scan -> signals/scan.py:47 _has_enabled_rules -> db/ai_tables.py:1139 list_rules -> :116 init_ai_tables -> conn.execute, synchronous on the event loop; at the open this contends with busy writers and parks the whole loop (httpx completion burst visible right after recovery). Same shape as the 07-21 pipeline_audit fix (sync sweep inline on loop -> to_thread). Fix sketch: to_thread the scan's DB reads and/or stop re-running init_ai_tables on every scan tick (module-level once-flag). NOT the 30-41s class (extinct 07-21) -- this is a distinct 2-7s open-hours class the probe now exposes.

[2026-07-27 SHIPPED] Full diagnosis overturned the first read. Stall counts/day: 19 (07-21), 14 (07-22), 271 (07-23), 479 (07-24) -- the explosion dates to 07-23, same day the quote-stream flaps and news db-locked errors began: ONE congestion event, three symptoms. Thread-attributed every caught stack today (probe dumps ALL threads; first histogram was contaminated -- fusion intake_once/_rescore is correctly in a worker thread, NOT a stall cause). Verified MainThread blockers: (1) init_ai_tables 14/31 -- called by ~every accessor in db/ai_tables (34 sites), body takes a WRITE txn (research_artifacts backfill) every call; fixed with once-per-process guard keyed on db_path, set only after success. (2) ai/perception/context.py build_symbol_context ran sync score_symbol inline -- ~800 days of bars for symbol AND SPY, network + SQLite cache write, on the loop (stack: ticker_routes _facts -> build_symbol_context -> score_symbol -> get_daily_bars -> cache_bars); fixed with to_thread. (3) signals/scan.py run_signal_scan sync DB reads on loop; fixed with to_thread. Remaining minor blockers seen once each (db/notifications, save_snapshot_analytics on loop) -- left, revisit if the probe still fires. VERIFY: loop_probe stall rate over the rest of today's session + tomorrow's open.
