cards.title: Options lane — the wheel + covered calls as automated portfolio strats (full ambition, staged by broker tiers + proof)
cards.notes:
Founder 07-19 (correcting the first capture): 'These safety rules are made up. We are going to do everything… just need to make sure it's implemented correctly.' Gates = (1) correct implementation (chokepoint/RiskEngine/paper-first extends to options, never shrinks ambition), (2) broker permission tiers (naked short options blocked at most account levels anyway -> hedged/defined-risk = the practical universe for now), (3) proven before armed (his words: 'we still have to prove this would even work'). FLAGSHIP: the wheel (cash-secured puts -> assignment -> covered calls) as an automated strategy — low broker tier, ships via the strategy framework (disarmed, founder arms, per-strat caps/attribution). Covered calls = natural first increment of the same lane. When-gates mechanical + LLM veto (IV rank vs own history, NO earnings inside expiry via EDGAR, shares/cash coverage, strike vs basis); every idea ledger-graded (premium kept vs upside forgone / assignment outcomes). Agent explains every structure plainly (max profit/loss, assignment, why-now) — the explanation IS the product; founder: with an advisor pointing him right + managing the trade, he'd feel better; possibly the most valued part of the app. ⚠️ Execution chokepoint is EQUITY-ONLY today — options execution = its own increment (RiskEngine assignment/expiry model, Alpaca options PAPER first, dual adversarial review, propose-only, off-by-default). ⚠️ Design round must FORMALLY REVISE the June no-agent-shorts decision record (SHORT_TRADING_FINDINGS.md) — option structures embed short exposure; founder 07-19: not afraid of selling short. Memory: options-strategies-direction.

2026-07-19 IV data-quality gate sharpened (founder q: why a second opinion when we have OPRA?): OPRA carries trades+quotes ONLY — every IV/greek is VENDOR-COMPUTED model output (their inverted price, rates, dividend/American-exercise treatment, snapshot timing). Since the lane's trigger is IV-rank, vendor artifacts = real-money bugs (momentum data-gate class). Primary check = SELF-COMPUTED IV from snapshot bid/ask mids (binomial for American singles) — our model, consistent history; vendor-vs-ours divergence is the alarm. Schwab IV cross-check demoted to optional; Schwab's unique value = strategy-chain spread pricing only.

2026-07-19: IV-rank history may be BACKFILLABLE for free — founder found the DoltHub post-no-preference/options dataset (2019->present daily IV/greeks, 1,532 names, verified live); see dolthub-options-history card for the validate+import round. Forward self-collection still runs (validation pair + OI which the dataset lacks).

2026-07-25 GATE ANSWERED -- NO. The pre-registered IV-rank baseline study ran (References/IV_RANK_BASELINE_PREREG_2026-07-25.md + ADDENDUM_A; BUILD_LOG row). Verdict: this lane does NOT open on a variance-risk-premium premise, and an IV-rank ENTRY GATE is not supported. H1 (premise) failed: mean VRP +0.0205 vol pts, month-block CI [-0.0015, +0.0373]. H2/H3 passed loudly (top-minus-bottom decile +0.0807, Spearman +1.000) and the pre-registered confound test then killed it: sorting by IV LEVEL is equally monotone (+1.000), and in a 5x5 level x rank double sort the rank effect does not survive holding level fixed (pooled within-level +0.0061 CI [-0.0268,+0.0323]; -0.0473 over 7 years) and REVERSES in low-vol names -- inside a quiet name a high IV rank means vol is rising for a reason. Most decision-relevant: on the 37 symbols we would actually trade there is NO VRP (H1 -0.0012), and the control shows the gap vs the corpus is the UNIVERSE (a high-vol curated tail we don't trade), not the horizon. Long-run context: a broad VRP does exist (+0.0306 excluding Feb-Apr 2020) but that one nine-week crash erases ~2 years of it -- precisely the tail a wheel is short. Card stays BACKLOG, now with a measured reason rather than an assumption. If revisited, pre-register the LEVEL axis fresh with the crash tail priced in, not averaged away; do NOT re-open from the headline decile table, which is confounded.

2026-07-25 STUDY B (the LEVEL axis) RAN -- effect is REAL, still not building, and the blocker moved. See References/IV_LEVEL_PREREG_2026-07-25.md. B1 PASS: top IV-level decile VRP +0.0944 CI [+0.0581,+0.1288] over 7 years, +0.1125 excluding Feb-Apr 2020. B2 PASS and it is the exact mirror of what killed rank: level orders VRP inside EVERY rank quintile (pooled +0.0857 CI [+0.0604,+0.1193]). B3 PASS both halves -- BETWEEN/selection +0.0736, WITHIN/timing +0.0858 -- which against rank's failure isolates something sharp: the MAGNITUDE of the deviation from a name's own normal is informative where the ORDINAL rank of it is not (95th percentile can sit 5% or 300% above average; bounded rank stats throw away the part that works). B4 FAIL is why nothing gets built: on our own 37 tradable names top-decile VRP is -0.0004 CI [-0.0269,+0.0253]. Diagnostic: the UNIVERSE binds, not the vol ceiling -- all names under 60% IV still passes (+0.0418 CI [+0.0168,+0.0630], 2,112 symbols), our 37 with no ceiling fails. So premium selling needs materially more BREADTH than the watchlist; the chain sampler's append-only universe is the natural vehicle and costs nothing to widen. B5 FAIL as written but B5 was itself the broken instrument (POST-RUN NOTE on the prereg): dropping the global top 5% of VRP removed 31.6% of the top decile because VRP correlates with the sort axis -- a symmetric 5%/5% trim leaves +0.0586, so outlier-robustness is UNTESTED, not disproven. Pre-registered consequences honored: B4 fail -> record and stop; B5 fail -> gates nothing. Card stays BACKLOG. Successor work, now specific: widen the universe, and model the CAPPED PAYOFF directly (a seller keeps at most the premium while the left tail is uncapped, so mean-VRP overstates capture however it is trimmed).

2026-07-25 STUDY C PRE-REGISTERED + RAN --References/IV_HORIZON_BREADTH_PREREG_2026-07-25.md. Study A's H4 arm (forward RV from OUR bars, 21 sessions, instead of the vendor's 30-session hv_current) ran on 37 symbols -- not a data limit, the code just sourced its symbol list from the sampler universe of the day. Alpaca serves daily bars for any ticker, so the cap was an implementation choice. That leaves the horizon x universe 2x2 with one empty cell: wide+vendor +0.0205, narrow+vendor -0.0105, narrow+own -0.0012, wide+own UNMEASURED. C1 fills it; C2 tests whether the horizon choice is material at all (<= 0.0100 vol pts) on the same (symbol,date) rows; C3/C4 re-run the LEVEL axis and the +0.0418 tradable band at the better horizon; C5 reports the deep tier for the record -- registering ~1,800 corpus names as a WIDE COLLECTION tier widened what we OBSERVE, not what we TRADE, so B4's null on our own names is not superseded. C6 pre-registers the bias this design introduces and it cuts the flattering way: a live bar API cannot serve a delisted ticker, and bankrupt names realize enormous vol (large negative VRP), so their absence biases mean VRP UP -- measured on the vendor panel where both groups exist, flagged above 0.0100. Cannot open the lane either way: the capped-payoff modelling remains the blocker.

2026-07-25 STUDY C RESULTS (1,602,950 obs / 2,200 symbols / 118,608 symbol-months / 2020-01-06 to 2026-06-23; bars for 2,285 of 2,311 corpus symbols). C1 PASS +0.0259 CI [+0.0047,+0.0428] full, +0.0363 [+0.0251,+0.0462] ex-2020 -- but KNIFE-EDGE, not a rescue of H1: Addendum A1's comparable 7-year vendor panel gave +0.0202 CI [-0.0018,+0.0371] (FAIL), and C1's interval is the same WIDTH shifted up ~+0.0057, matching C2's measured horizon effect of +0.0051. A verdict that flips on 0.005 vol pts is not robust; only the ex-2020 arm is non-marginal. C2 PASS gap 0.0051 on 634,118 paired (symbol,date) rows -> horizon immaterial to magnitude, confirming 'universe not horizon' at breadth. C3 PASS Spearman +1.000 monotone across all ten level deciles (-0.0067 at mean IV 0.192 -> +0.0909 at 0.833). C4 PASS +0.0445 CI [+0.0178,+0.0661] on 2,083 symbols under the 60% ceiling vs Study B's +0.0418 -- the tradable-band figure SURVIVES the horizon correction. C5 descriptive and unchanged: our 37 deep-tier names -0.0012 CI [-0.0198,+0.0154], in-band -0.0035. C6 flagged but HOLLOW -- its premise ('a live bar API cannot serve a delisted ticker') is empirically false: BBBY 1,718 bars, WOLF 1,718, FRC 907, SIVB 872, so the blowups are IN the panel; the flag rests on 5 symbols vs 2,200 and those 5 had HIGHER VRP (+0.0583), so the bias runs against the result. ** THE NEW GATE, and it is this round's real output: C4's wide band (+0.0445) and C5's own-names band (-0.0035) sit at nearly identical implied vol -- mean IV 0.554 vs 0.547. Same vol level, opposite sign, so the discriminator is WHICH NAMES, not what IV (intervals overlap slightly -- suggestive, not decisive). Natural hypothesis: competition. Our watchlist is megacap + index ETFs, the most heavily option-sold instruments on earth; the corpus tail is not. If that is the mechanism it is BAD news -- options are rich where few people sell them, which is where the bid-ask is widest, and every number in Studies A/B/C is vendor MID-market IV that ignores the spread entirely. So premium selling now has TWO untested gates: the capped payoff AND the spread in exactly the names that carry the premium. Card stays BACKLOG.

2026-07-25 the SPREAD gate is now probed -- see card option-spread-gate. Band names cost 0.0870 vol pts to cross once (195% of the +0.0445 edge) vs 0.0292 for ours: ~3.2x more expensive, competition hypothesis confirmed in direction. (!) NOT a finding yet -- Saturday closing quotes, and the prereg made PROHIBITIVE non-decisive; intraday re-run required. The capped-payoff gate remains completely untouched.

cards.title: SPX structural strikes — gamma-wall/collar overlay + pre-registered magnet study
cards.notes:
Founder 07-19: SPX whale prints are largely structural (JPM/JHEQX quarterly collar class — known strikes, rolled quarterly at Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec ends) and act as magnets + S/R as far as he's seen; wants them MARKED — a chart study on SPX, another angle for trade ideas. Two phases, measurement first: (1) MAGNET STUDY — pre-register metrics (print-lab pattern, prereg = LAW) for pin/magnet behavior: distance-to-top-OI-strike into expiry vs control days, on chain snapshots the index chain sampler already collects daily; (2) CHART STUDY — top-OI strike rails + known-collar annotations + roll-date calendar rendered by our chart engine (top-toolbar control, plain lowercase labels, no pills); overlay states what the study MEASURED, never folklore ('magnet' label only if phase 1 validates). If validated, the tradeable framing is REVERSION (founder 07-19): entry = price EXTENDED away from the validated magnet (displacement band from measured reversion-onset percentile), target = the strike, stop = measured reversion-FAILURE percentile — a fully deterministic plan authored by the study, no LLM levels. Study axes: displacement x time-to-expiry x standing OI, ALWAYS against current OI (roll calendar load-bearing — stale strikes are dead magnets). Magnet BREAK with OI standing = its own trend signal, registered not discarded. Both directions measured; above-magnet (downward-pull) setups surface as perception only — chokepoint stays long-only. Related: flow_decomp hedge-block reads (classifies these prints as structural), index-0dte-concentration-study (adjacent strike-concentration machinery), options-flow-academic-prior memory (whale prints = hedging, not informed flow).

2026-07-19 (founder): proximity-to-magnet DOES have edge — as a VOLATILITY trade: pinning = collapsed realized movement near the strike -> sell premium centered there (just-OTM call+put). Study gains a second pre-registered output: how tightly price holds AT the magnet (prices the strangle), alongside reversion-from-displacement. Expression = DEFINED-RISK structures only, and only after the options lane exists (see options-income-lane card) — naked short strangles never.

2026-07-19 (founder, composition): named test candidates once the pin range is validated — (a) ~30d to opex + reversion expected toward the collar -> covered calls at/above the magnet strike; (b) short straddle/strangle centered on the expected landing range near the collar. The study's pin-tightness output IS the range width that prices both. Hedged/defined-risk expressions per broker tiers; builds on the options lane (options-income-lane / options-expression-selection). 07-19 UNBLOCKED for backtesting: SPX-complex daily OI history OWNED (Databento statistics 2013-2023 + 2025-now, data/databento/, ~199M records; see dolthub-options-history card for purchase detail). The magnet/pin study can now run historically, not just forward; decode into a queryable per-day per-strike OI store = first step of the study round. 07-19 first empirical read of the purchased OI: JHEQX collar CONFIRMED in 2022 data (2022-10-03, Dec-30 expiry: P3390/C3835/P2860 at ~44.5k each, next strike 19k - textbook 5%/20%/7% geometry vs 3586 close) but the classic quarter-end triple is ABSENT mid-2026 (Sep-30-2026 max ~13k, no triple, checked 3 weeks of July) - consistent with the reported post-front-running evolution of the JPM complex (staggered funds/laddered rolls). DESIGN LAW: wall detection must be GENERIC (OI-vs-strike-neighborhood unusualness, persistence tracking), never hardcoded collar shapes. Processing plan: condense 199M recs -> (date,root,expiry,strike,cp,oi) store -> generic wall detector -> prereg'd pin/magnet metrics vs null baselines -> products only on pass. 07-20 collar timeline DATED from all six 2025-26 rolls: triple visible every quarter through Jan-2026 roll (leg sizes shrinking 40k->37.8k->35.6k->35.0k through 2025) then VANISHED at exactly the Mar-31-2026 roll (Apr/Jul 2026 quarter-ends: no triple, max 11-13k). Reads as deliberate migration (laddering/sister funds/FLEX/OTC), not exit. Named study task: hunt the migrated footprint (new ~30k-class OI clusters around 2026-03-31, any root/expiry). Corpus upside: 13yrs of collar-in-full-bloom = known-wall backtest ground truth. 07-20 migration CONFIRMED by external reporting (Substack 'The Whale Changed Lanes', corroborates our OPRA finding independently): at the Mar-31-2026 roll the collar re-established same-day in CME's S&P 500 Month-End options (SME, launched 2025 - 4pm cash-close settle kills NAV tracking error, American exercise, BTIC execution kills order-book front-running). Q2-2026 structure reported: 6180/5210 put spread + 6865 short call. => OPRA footprint hunt is MOOT (position left OPRA universe); tracking the new home needs CME GLBX options-on-futures statistics (Databento carries it - quote when study earns it; SME chain is new+thin so its OI may BE the collar, cleaner than SPX ever was). Bonus: viral X bot's 'confirmed Q2-2026 strikes' (5905/5310/4480) = EXACTLY our Apr-2025 legs - recycled year-old data, debunked by our own OI. 07-20 WHALE REACQUIRED in SME data ($0.20 purchase, founder topped up + authorized): SMEM6 P6180/C6865/P5210 at EXACTLY 31,000 each = the Substack's reported Q2 structure, confirmed in our own OI. BEYOND the reporting: the NEXT quarter already stands (SMEU6 Sep: P7090/C7890/P5990 at 24,800) and MONTHLY ~8k triples ride alongside (SMEJ6 8.2k / SMEK6 3.9k / SMEN6 Jul 6830/5760/7565 at 8.1k = the staggered sister funds JHQDX/JHQTX). The whole hedged-equity complex is visible in a thin chain where it IS most of the OI. Live wall map restored for current trading: Jul 8.1k triple + Sep 24.8k triple. Study tasks: date the 2025 migration start in SME (data begins 2025-09-22); fold SME walls into the generic detector alongside OPRA history. 07-20 STAGE 1 DONE (tools/oi_condense.py): 27,221,980 rows condensed into data/oi_walls.db (3.7GB, (date,source,root,expiry,cp,strike,oi), 2013-04-01 -> 2026-07-17, OPRA + SME). Landmarks verified: 2022-10-03 collar legs exact (44547/44500/44500 @ P3390/P2860/C3835); SME Jun-2026 triple 30499/leg. BONUS dating: SME options OI begins 2025-11-19 = the migration's actual start. Next: generic wall detector + prereg doc.

Flow-lane ideas grade at short horizons.\n\n[2026-07-26 audit round] (!) CORRECTS THE PREMISE OF THIS CARD. 'Pushes are dead' is WRONG -- measured 75 'Sent alert push' lines in 3 days of hmt-backend journal: idea-triggered, price alerts, the Idea Engine canary, and all three LLM books all reached the phone on 07-24. Only the convergence/solo FLOW rows are dead (the 07-21/22 founder order), and only those were ever budget-gated. cards.title: Intraday position-watch — event-gated LLM wake-ups + order-management verbs (agent-awareness layer)
cards.notes: Design captured 2026-07-24 (founder discussion; not started). PROBLEM: the nightly book cycle is a script that dies overnight — nothing manages open positions intraday; exits/optimization happen only at night, and a thesis formed at 5pm executes ~16h later at a gap-risk open. GOAL = the 'agent aware of its own positions' layer, as two typed nodes on the book graph: (Aggregator) an EVENT-GATED position-watch = PERCEIVE, and (Sink) ORDER-MANAGEMENT VERBS (cancel/replace/exit through the chokepoint) = ACT. ⚠️ VERBS ARE THE PREREQUISITE — build the ability to act before the trigger to act on, or it's just a smarter pager (today: interim holds_review, founder acts manually). Absorbs the 'NEXT INCREMENT: analyst order-management verbs' item from [[llm-books-program]]; relates to stop-lifecycle-v2. ── GATING MECHANICS (the hard part, solved in discussion): do NOT gate on a static threshold — gate on decision-relevant CHANGE. (1) EDGE-trigger not level-trigger: fire on the transition INTO a danger zone and consume it, don't re-fire while the condition stays true. (2) HYSTERESIS / Schmitt trigger: arm ~1.5% from stop, disarm only after recovery past ~3% — kills the 'price hovers just above stop all day' chatter. (3) The LLM AUTHORS ITS OWN RE-ARM CONDITION each wake ('hold unless price breaks 312 OR vol >3x on a down bar OR a downgrade prints') → the cheap loop then watches THAT narrower tripwire; the gate self-sharpens per wake (the 'rejected-idea-writes-a-rule' loop applied to monitoring). (4) NEWS gated by materiality x price-confirmation: dedup/cluster (50 rewrites=1 event), primary-catalyst-class only (earnings/guidance/downgrade/M&A/SEC/FDA, not 'analyst reiterates'), AND require an abnormal price/vol move — news alone is LOGGED as position context, never a wake; price is the arbiter of whether news mattered. Solves 'headlines all day that do nothing to price' by construction. (5) HARD BUDGET CAP per position/day → on breach, batch into ONE 'X is unusually active, auto-watch paused' push to founder, never a token spend-spiral. ── SHIPPING PHILOSOPHY (founder call 07-24, 'too many things in shadow mode'): PERCEIVE+PROPOSE ships LIVE now with sane defaults + the cap (downside is cheap — tokens/notifications, bounded by cap), tune from real behavior; NO shadow-mode study. The ONLY rung that earns a measured proving period is the propose→AUTO-EXIT flip (expensive/irreversible = real money + trust; autonomy ladder). Test for shadow-mode = 'is being wrong expensive AND irreversible?' — the wake-up gate is neither. Downside is ALSO already covered intraday by resting GTC stops (broker-enforced in RTH) → the watch is OPTIMIZATION not blowup-prevention, which is why it can stay cheap + event-gated. ── RELATED (same discussion, own follow-up): make the nightly panel judge BLIND to the analyst's rhetoric/self-graded win% — re-derive its own verdict from data + the pre-registered rubric (maker-checker; the Fable judge is the MOST capable model, correct for this seat — see [[agent-model-budget-routing]]). ── SEQUENCE: (a) management verbs behind the chokepoint (adversarial review — trading/ safety), (b) event-gated watch on the existing backend poll loop in PROPOSE mode + defaults + cap, (c) tune triggers from live behavior, (d) later: propose→auto-exit after a measured track record. Graph vocabulary borrowed from the 'graph engineering' pattern (worker/validator/aggregator/sink) but NO framework migration — deprioritized plumbing per mission; use patterns we already have (Workflow harness, poll loop, cron).

cards.title: Whole-market OPRA directional-flow corpus — the 1,000-sub cap bought out for $199/mo
cards.notes:
Founder subscribed Databento Standard 2026-07-26. Verified by get_cost, not assumed: whole-market OPRA tcbbo 12mo went $36,779.72 -> $0.00; L1 window is EXACTLY 12 months and ROLLS DAILY (18mo still quotes $14,964.49), so days not archived before they age out become a purchase -- the backfill has a deadline, not just a cost. L0 (statistics/ohlcv/definition) is free to 2013, which retroactively zeroes the $51,659 full-universe OI quote BUILD_LOG 07-19 recorded as dead.
WHY IT MATTERS: our own lane resolves direction on 57.4% of events and is 41.8% BLIND in the opening 30min (anchor warm-up), across ~21 contracts on 40 names. tcbbo attaches the NBBO at print time: 89.0% of prints / 92.7% of premium classified, FLAT across the session (58.1% open vs 57.3% rest), on every contract of every name. The anchor/hot-pool/promotion tuning that was queued before this is now DEAD WORK -- do not build it.
Shipped this round: tools/opra_tcbbo_backfill.py (resumable, per-day cost guard aborts above --max-cost, default $0.00 -- the $43 overage of 07-19 had no funds pre-check), db/flow_corpus.py + tools/flow_corpus_rollup.py (11s/session on numpy; pandas rejected because serv had 6GB free while holding the OPRA socket), tools/flow_corpus_bars.py (Alpaca, recursive bisection on 400).
MEASURED, decides an open question: unserved-by-Alpaca premium is 30.8% and it is ENTIRELY index roots (SPX/SPXW/NDX/VIX/RUT) that NO equity vendor serves. Delisted equities are $11M of $45,573M = 0.02%. => the $4.82 Databento point-in-time backfill buys nothing. NOT buying.
Open: backfill completing (~260 sessions); index-root spot needs a proxy or stays 'unknown' (prereg's secondary arm excludes index roots anyway); 0.37% unresolved prints CLOSED (all instrument 5930 / BBX / class 'K' INDEX; the C/P filter is also the only thing stopping their size==UINT32_MAX from inflating a session ~9.2e8x).
Addendum B (07-26): spot-reference rule pinned — historic AND live both use the PRIOR-SESSION split-adjusted close, even live, because a reference change at the historic->live seam fabricates a change event on every underlying at once. Spot source is part of schema_version; changing it is a full re-roll (raw prints retained so it stays a re-roll, not a re-purchase). Index spot DEFERRED as a decision: Databento sells us no index dataset (29 available, none index); put-call parity from our own prints recovers SPX 7,484.30 / NDX 28,524.55 / RUT 2,942.73 but at +-0.4-1.3% crude, too loose for a 2% bucket boundary until done per-expiry and time-matched.
LIVE SWAP built 2026-07-26 (founder: 'retire a databento module so we could easily swap back' — Alpaca is NOT deleted): signals/options_flow/dbn_stream.py duck-types OptionsFlowStream's surface (collected_prints/quote_at/acked_market_wide/run/stop), reuses normalize_print so the print shape is identical, and quote_at returns the print's OWN attached NBBO — zero staleness, no quote cache, no anchors, no hot pool. Selected by settings options_flow.provider, DEFAULT 'alpaca' (ships off, armed deliberately, per strategy-off-by-default). NO auto-fallback either direction: a dead session logs loud and stops, because silently degrading to the worse source is the exact shape that left the copilot web-blind 3x. direction_basis='dbn_nbbo' stamped per print (runner.py now reads quote_basis off the print instead of hard-coding 'stream_quote') so post-swap events never pool with the Alpaca era in options_flow_events. ONE variable changes: same watchlist (parent-symbol subscribe), same detectors, same thresholds — widening to whole-market is a separate step or a regression cannot be attributed. Live entitlement probed OK (parent stype accepted, session opened/closed clean). 5 new tests; 2,784 passing.
⏳ NOT ARMED — do not flip options_flow.provider until the backfill lands and the provider is verified against a session whose ground truth we already hold.
⚠️ DEFINITION PULL WAS BROKEN — found + fixed 07-26 while recovering the crashed session. The per-date ET session window was applied to EVERY schema, including `definition`. Definitions are a START-OF-DAY SNAPSHOT, not intraday events, so any window not starting at UTC midnight returns only contracts newly listed inside it. Databento warns on this explicitly and we were ignoring it. Measured, OPRA.PILLAR ALL_SYMBOLS 2025-07-28: ET window = 0.1 MB billable / 285 records vs full UTC day = 575.4 MB / 1,598,325 records — a 5,754x under-pull, both quoted $0.00. Since ALL_SYMBOLS files ship no symbology mappings, definition is the ONLY instrument_id -> underlying/strike/expiry/right resolver: the corpus would have completed ~57 GB of prints that resolve to NOTHING, looking finished on disk the whole time. Fixed by branching the window per schema (_definition_bounds_utc vs _session_bounds_utc); re-pull of 2025-07-28 verified 285 -> 1,598,325 records, warning gone. The 8 truncated defs files were deleted so they re-pull (the skip guard is size>0, and 7 KB passes it — they would have been skipped forever).
⚠️ AND THE REVIEWERS' DST FIX HAD NEVER SHIPPED. tools/opra_tcbbo_backfill.py existed as TWO divergent copies: the one actually executed (dev/help_me_trade, UNTRACKED on main) carried the corrected ET bounds, while the TRACKED copy on this branch still had the original RTH=('T13:30','T20:00') fixed UTC slice. The live run was correct so nothing looked wrong — a silent-success one level up from the class this card keeps hitting. Both fixes are now in the tracked copy.
Resumed 07-26 19:47 via tools/opra_backfill_run.sh — setsid-detached so it survives the session, nice+ionice, defs THEN tcbbo sequentially (two concurrent ALL_SYMBOLS pulls is what helped swap the box flat). Progress: tail data/databento/run.log. At restart: tcbbo 26/260, defs 2/260.
Open: backfill completing (~260 sessions x2); tcbbo BBO semantics STILL UNSETTLED — is the attached quote the one prevailing immediately BEFORE the print? Three reviewers were killed mid-flight before answering; partial finding is that `action` surfaces as `_reserved1` (84='T') with bid_pb/ask_pb present. Re-run ONE reviewer at a time, not three concurrent Opus agents against a 258 MB file.
✅ tcbbo BBO SEMANTICS SETTLED 07-26 — the quote is PRE-TRADE. Vendor's own words, read out of the installed databento_dbn package rather than scraped: TCBBO = "consolidated best bid and offer trade record containing the consolidated BBO before the trade"; sibling TBBO = "All trade events with the best bid and offer (BBO) immediately **before** the effect of the trade" (Databento's own emphasis). Corroborated empirically on TWO sessions (tools/tcbbo_semantics_probe.py, 14.3M prints, 2025-08-26 + 2025-08-28): 62.9%/63.2% of prints sit exactly AT the touch, while only 0.38-0.51% print above the ask and 0.45-0.50% below the bid — a post-trade book would have moved away and could not concentrate mass on the touch like that. Decisive corroborator: ~26% of at-ask prints carry size >= the displayed ask size (2.4-2.6% strictly exceed it), which is contradictory under a post-trade quote — the book cannot still be showing an offer the print already consumed. Founder's 99% recollection was right.
⚠️ BUT: THE QUOTE IS ONE SNAPSHOT PER SWEEP, NOT PER LEG. 99.4% of multi-print groups sharing an (instrument_id, ts_event) carry an IDENTICAL bid/ask. So every leg of a sweep is signed against the same pre-sweep quote — correct as a direction reference, but N legs are NOT N independent quote observations, and book-walking depth cannot be inferred from the attached BBO. Any statistic that weights by print count across a sweep is double-counting one observation.
⚠️ ALSO MEASURED: the `side` field is 'N' on 100% of prints (all 14.3M) — OPRA never populates it, so direction is quote-derived by necessity, not by choice. And ~37% of prints fall STRICTLY INSIDE the spread, unsignable by the touch test; the 89.0%-classified figure must lean on a midpoint/tick rule for that third — confirm which, and how exact-mid prints are handled, before the study reads through it.
✅ THE 0.37% UNRESOLVED PRINTS ARE EXPLAINED (07-26) — close that open question. On 2025-07-28 the join drops 24,298 prints = 0.3494%, and they are ALL one instrument: instrument_id 5930, raw_symbol BBX, instrument_class 'K' (INDEX), with UNDEF strike and UNDEF expiration. _load_definitions already keeps only 'C'/'P', so class-K never enters d_ids and every one of its prints is dropped by the join. Dropping them is CORRECT — they are not options. Also note they carry size == UINT32_MAX (the DBN unset sentinel), so had they survived the join, `premium = price/PX * size * 100` would have inflated session premium ~918,000,000x ($26.3B -> $24.2 QUINTILLION). The C/P filter is the only thing preventing that: it is load-bearing and non-obvious, so do NOT relax the join to 'recover' unresolved prints without adding an explicit size-sentinel guard first.
CLASSIFIER AUDIT, post-join, the numbers the corpus actually stores (tools/flow_classifier_audit.py, 2025-07-28, 6,930,544 prints after join): side-classified = 87.83% (docstring says ~89%; buy 42.29% / sell 45.54%), at-mid-unsigned 10.06%, good_q 97.89%, unquoted 1.22%, locked 0.88%, crossed 0.01%. Strict/touch rule signs only 61.9% and leaves 36.01% inside. Premium clean at $26,310,928,243.
⛔ REAL DEFECT — u_prem's SIGN IS SET BY 0.40% OF PRINTS. `u = (price-mid)/half` is UNBOUNDED (measured range [-61, +90]) and u_prem is a premium-weighted SUM. Prints with |u|>2 are 0.40% of the corpus but contribute 171.92% of sum(u*premium): total = +366,445,672 while the |u|>2 tail alone = +629,989,228, so the other 99.6% of prints sum to -263,543,556. The aggregate reads BULLISH while the bulk of flow leans BEARISH, purely on outliers. Any 'flow leaned long/short' read off u_prem is an artifact until u is bounded (winsorize or clip to [-1,1]) or u_prem is stored alongside a robust counterpart. ⚠️ u is a PRE-REGISTERED metric — changing its definition post-hoc is a prereg violation, so this is a founder decision, NOT an agent fix.
⚠️ minor: rollup line 158 nan_to_num(u, nan=0.0) maps bad-quote prints onto u=0.0, which is exactly the value meaning 'printed at the midpoint' — 0.54% of premium is folded into at-mid rather than excluded. ⚠️ minor: rollup line 123 does to_ndarray() with NO chunking, materializing a whole session (~500MB raw + float64 copies) before the 260-session run; the audit/probe tools chunk at 1M records for this reason.
✅ u_premium_clipped SHIPPED 07-26 (SCHEMA_VERSION 1->2, ALTER-migrated; v1 rows read as not-ingested so they re-roll). The pre-registered u_premium is stored UNCHANGED; the clipped counterpart is the labelled post-hoc robustness check. Same doctrine the rollup docstring already applied to midpoint-vs-strict: write both so neither can be chosen after seeing results. Verified end-to-end on 2025-07-28 (140,996 rows) and it reproduces the file-level audit exactly: u_raw +366.5M, u_clip +95.4M.
★ HOW TO READ DIRECTION — three measures, agreement is the rule. (1) NET PREMIUM (buy minus sell) is the robust leg and needs NO new column, it is already implied by the `side` key: each print contributes at most its own premium with a sign, so it is outlier-immune by construction. (2) u_premium_clipped. (3) u_premium raw. MEASURED bucket-level agreement on 2025-07-28 across 45,384 buckets: all three agree on 92.15% of BUCKETS but only 75.33% of PREMIUM; u_raw vs u_clip disagree on just 0.24% of buckets yet those carry 15.8% of premium. ⚠️ THE FRAGILITY IS CONCENTRATED WHERE THE MONEY IS — a count-weighted check would have called this a non-issue. Operating rule: require all three to agree, else ABSTAIN (~25% of premium). Session-level the measures agreed on both sessions tested (2025-07-28 all bullish: net +$553M / u_raw +366M / u_clip +95M; 2026-07-23 bearish: net -$1,025M / u_raw -846M).
CORRECTIONS to the earlier audit row, both overstated: (a) nan_to_num(u, nan=0.0) does NOT corrupt u_premium — u=0 contributes exactly 0.0 to the SUM (verified identical: 366,445,672 both ways). It is a DENOMINATOR hygiene issue only: dividing by a premium total that includes bad-quote prints biases the mean toward zero by their 0.54% weight. (b) Clipping does NOT flip the session-level sign; it changes MAGNITUDE 3.84x (366.4M -> 95.4M). The real risk is per-bucket, quantified above.

cards.title: EDGAR acceptanceDateTime's `Z` is inconsistently ET — session_hour() mislabels AMC filers as dmh, and the test enshrines it
cards.notes:
FOUND 2026-07-30 by a founder check against price action, not by reading code. I claimed AMZN's earnings 8-K was public at 12:06 ET (from the submissions JSON's "2026-07-30T16:06:23.000Z"); founder said the stock popped after 4pm, not at lunch. The tape settled it: AMZN 16:01 ET 236.00 -> 248.70; at 12:06 it was 238.92 -> 238.97 on 148k shares. Nothing.

THE DEFECT. `data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK*.json` `acceptanceDateTime` carries a `Z` suffix whose value is SOMETIMES Eastern and sometimes genuine UTC. Measured on 18 earnings 8-Ks across 6 mega-caps against EDGAR's own `ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME` header (always ET): 8 of 18 are unconverted ET-with-Z. NOT a clean date cutoff — MSFT (x3) and JPM (x3) are unconverted across six months while NVDA (x3) and WMT (x3) are correct over the same span; AAPL and AMZN were correct in Jan/Apr and unconverted on 07-30. Cause unknown; candidates are per-filer behaviour and/or a change from ~07-29 onward. Either way the field cannot be used: blanket-converting mislabels MSFT/JPM by 4-5h, reading raw mislabels NVDA/WMT by 4-5h.

GROUND TRUTH (both verified against the tape): the native `ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME:` (ET, YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) in `Archives/edgar/data/<cik>/<accession>/<accession>-index-headers.html`, or the HTTP `Last-Modified` on any document in the filing folder (true GMT). AMZN: JSON 16:06:23Z / native 20260730160623 ET / Last-Modified 20:06:45 GMT / move at 16:01 ET. MSFT 2026-07-29 confirms independently: native 16:04 ET, +2.97% at 16:01 ET, flat at 12:04.

THE FIX. `signals/earnings_edgar.py:141 session_hour()` docstring asserts "The stamps are UTC" and blanket-converts, so AMC filers come out `dmh` (AMZN, AAPL, MSFT all mislabeled). Either source the hour from the native header (one extra request per filing) or drop the hour rather than emit a wrong one. `tests/test_earnings_edgar.py:68 test_session_hour_converts_utc_to_eastern` LOCKS IN the bad assumption — the suite is not a check on this and must be rewritten with the fix.

BLAST RADIUS is small, which is luck not design: the persisted `data/research/earnings.db` stores only (symbol, cik, date) — no hour — so the 185k-row corpus is clean; only the live in-memory `hour` field from `parse_recent_earnings` is wrong. Note this error runs OPPOSITE to the bias already documented in the edgar-free-earnings-source memory (which says EDGAR reports the session LATER than truth); that one-way characterisation is now incomplete.

METHOD NOTE worth keeping: a timestamp is not self-verifying. The only reason this surfaced is that the founder tested the claim against what the stock actually did. Any future latency/timing claim gets checked against the tape before it is recorded as fact.

=== FIXED 2026-07-31 (see BUILD_LOG 07-31) ===
Re-measured first, and found my own instrument was wrong: the earlier regex assumed `ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME:` but the header is `<ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME>`. The corrected run RE-CONFIRMS 8-of-18 (8 spurious-Z, 10 genuine UTC) — conclusion stood, method didn't.
BETTER FIX than this card proposed: the current-filings atom feed's <updated> carries an explicit offset, tracks DST (-05:00 in Feb), and agrees with the native ET header on BOTH filer kinds — NVDA reads 16:21:19-04:00 where the submissions JSON says 20:21:19Z, so the feed genuinely converts rather than re-stamping. Two trustworthy sources, and the atom one is free with detection.
session_hour() now REFUSES any Z-suffixed stamp BY SHAPE — datetime.fromisoformat accepts 'Z' happily, so rejecting only on parse failure would let the bug return silently. tests/test_earnings_edgar.py no longer enshrines the assumption; it pins the refusal.
OPEN: the calendar's `hour` from filings.recent is now honestly None. Restoring it via the per-company atom feed (one request per company returns up to 100 correctly-stamped filings) is the follow-up — tracked on edgar-calendar-hour-restore.

FOUNDER DIRECTION 2026-07-30: "it needs to work for every tracked stock, not just my watch list" and "I definitely want to store that full SEC EDGAR... so if I ask an agent any sort of question, they have every number to play with." Agreed and consistent with the standing rule that a watchlist is a runtime filter over fixed-cost feeds, never a design-time constant. You also cannot screen a universe you never ingested.

STARTING STATE (measured): `data/research/fundamentals.db` holds 3,921 companies (symbol->CIK->SIC->sector) and NOTHING else — `shares` 0 rows, `financials` 0 rows. `build_financials` has no cron and no backend caller, only a manual CLI flag, so the statement layer shipped wired-but-empty. Related honesty bug: for a symbol present in `companies`, `latest_financials` returns a row rather than None, so `_read_fundamentals`'s "not in the EDGAR cache — build it" hint never fires and the agent gets `metrics: {}` under a confident `source: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts` line. That reads as "this company reported nothing." Fix with the ingest. Also: `latest_financials` calls `_ensure_schema`, so a READ opens the store read-write and creates tables (observed).

ENDPOINTS (all sec.gov, free, keyless, sizes measured 07-30):
1. `Archives/edgar/daily-index/xbrl/companyfacts.zip` — 1.39 GB, rebuilt daily. One download replaces ~6,000 per-symbol calls and covers filers we never listed. serv has 467 GB free. Store ALL concepts (542 for AMZN), not the 12 we currently extract — the founder wants every number, disk is free, and re-deciding later costs another night. NOT into trading.db (2.4 GB money ledger) — its own research store.
2. `files/dera/data/financial-statement-data-sets/<Y>q<N>.zip` — 85 MB -> 559 MB num.txt, quarterly. This is the ONLY source of SEGMENTS: num.txt has a populated `segments` column (221,877 of the first 400k rows carry a dimension, e.g. `BusinessSegments=ClientAndGaming;ConsolidationItems=OperatingSegments`). companyfacts strips all dimensions — verified: 542 concepts for AMZN, not one is segment revenue, so "AWS grew X%" is absent from that feed by construction.
3. `cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcurrent&type=8-K&output=atom` — live filing feed, current to the minute (newest entry tracks the 17:30 ET cutoff, not staleness). Detection latency = our poll interval.

GOTCHAS, all measured: companyfacts is built from 10-K/10-Q XBRL ONLY (AMZN revenue = 48 10-K + 76 10-Q rows, ZERO 8-K), so an earnings release never lands there — a bulk rebuild timestamped minutes after a release is coincidence, not capture. NO Q4 QUARTER EXISTS (no 10-Q is filed for Q4; the 10-K carries the FY total) — AMZN's quarterly series runs Q1->Q2->Q3 then jumps to next year's Q1, so derive Q4 = FY - (Q1+Q2+Q3) or every quarterly YoY silently holes each December. Concept coverage varies by filer: AMZN tags no total `Liabilities` (derive assets - equity) and no `ResearchAndDevelopmentExpense`. Foreign private issuers file 6-K/20-F with no 10-Q at all (ASML/TSM-type names) — own branch or they go missing silently.

THE EXHIBIT READER is the piece with real value and real difficulty. The earnings release is furnished as 8-K Item 2.02 exhibit EX-99.1 — for AMZN 07-30 that was a 656 KB / ~44k-word document carrying AWS, North America, International, operating income, free cash flow AND forward guidance. We ALREADY locate these filings (earnings.db covers 3,120 symbols by scanning 8-K Item 2.02) and throw the attachment away, keeping only the date. So this is reading an envelope we already open, not a new pipeline. Store the raw exhibit permanently so a parser bug is re-runnable instead of a lost quarter; see the research-reader-is-the-weak-link memory — fetch_url is a regex tag-stripper and is NOT adequate for this.

HONEST FRAMING (corrected after the founder's price-action check): EDGAR is the COMPLETE source, NOT the fast one. Measured ladder on AMZN 07-30 — market moves 16:01, Benzinga headline 16:02:03, guidance headline 16:05:05, EDGAR exhibit 16:06:45, companyfacts ~2 days. Nobody in our stack wins the reaction window; even Benzinga trailed the tape by ~1 min. What EDGAR buys is completeness (whole document vs an editor's 3 headline strings over 23 min), coverage that is a legal obligation rather than a vendor's business decision (the thin tail of the 3,120 names is where an edge would live), and PIT-honest structure we can re-parse. Do NOT sell this as 'at release time'.

NOT MEASURED: the gap between EDGAR acceptance and public dissemination, and whether the ~5 min wire->EDGAR lead is stable across filers. Both are checkable against our own stored news (`news_items.published_at`/`received_at`) and should be, before anyone trades the gap. Depends on card `edgar-acceptance-hour-lies` for trustworthy timestamps.

WITHOUT ROWID PK (cik, concept_id, period_end, filed, unit, period_start, accn); (taxonomy,tag) interned; accn as int64. cards.title: ⚠️ Pending sells are accounted for ONLY from the last snapshot — two sells inside one poll window can oversell
cards.notes:
SHIPPED 2026-08-02. Two reduce-only sells inside one snapshot window each validated against the whole long -- reproduced as 12 shares sold against 10 held, which flips the account into an unintended SHORT. RiskEngine derived pending_sell SOLELY from snapshot['open_orders'], and for a sell-to-close exposure_increasing is False, so that snapshot figure was the ONLY quantity gate. The snapshot refreshes on the poll loop but validates for up to _SNAPSHOT_MAX_AGE = 5 MINUTES, so the window is minutes, not the 20s poll.

MECHANISM: db.order_executions.sum_inflight_sell_qty() -- the share-count twin of sum_inflight_notional -- consulted by the sell branch as a SEPARATE term (available = held - pending_sell - inflight_sell). A row is counted only when the snapshot cannot already account for it: no broker_order_id (bounded by _UNPLACED_RESERVATION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 120 so an abandoned submit cannot lock a position for good), or at the broker, absent from open_orders, AND submitted_at at/after captured_at. New occ_symbol column: order_executions.symbol holds the UNDERLYING for options, so keying on it alone would have been dead for option exits and would have cross-blocked equity vs option sells on one ticker; reservations key COALESCE(occ_symbol, symbol). symbol is now normalised at the write -- SQLite '=' is case-sensitive, so an un-normalised row was an invisible gate.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW EARNED ITS KEEP -- two Opus reviewers, split mandates, TWO ROUNDS. Round 1 found two HIGHs in the first cut, both CONFIRMED with running repros: (1) the dedup counted orders that had already FILLED, so the snapshot's already-reduced position was debited twice, and a stuck 'submitted' row locked a position PERMANENTLY -- measured against the live ledger, v1 would have locked AMZN 50 and GOOGL 61 on deploy (no exit AND no re-stop); (2) folding the reservation into blocked_by_pending_sells made a DB-only block trigger the stop-release path, which cancels live protection it cannot help. Round 2 found two more: (3) save_snapshot stamped captured_at at WRITE time, so an order placed between the broker fetch and the write was invisible to BOTH mechanisms -- captured_at is now stamped BEFORE the fetch and passed in by all three callers; (4) a release still destroyed a live stop when the reservation blocked the RESTORE, which asks for the stop's full size -- deterministic for a whole-position stop (Q=H fails for any I>0), giving a bare position + critical page. Fixed by reporting a block as releasable ONLY when the order would actually fit afterwards (qty <= held - inflight_sell), so a stop that cannot help is never taken down. Also: submitted_at only, never updated_at (every status write re-dates it, which dragged dead rows back into reserving); strict '<' on the timestamp tie so an exact tie counts.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, deliberate: test_a_genuine_oversell_does_not_release_anything asserted cancel-then-restore; it now asserts the stop is NEVER cancelled. Same end state, no unprotected window, no dependence on the restore.

VERIFY: ruff clean; 3,705 passed; 14 guards kill-switched RED->GREEN (one -- symbol normalisation -- had NO test until the mutation stayed green); both reviewers' own probe scripts re-run against the final tree.

KNOWN LIMIT (documented in the docstring, not a card): afetch_snapshot reads account/positions/orders concurrently, so a fill landing between the orders and positions reads leaves a stale-high position that can still be oversold -- pre-existing (_uncommitted_shares MEDIUM-1), neither introduced nor fixable here. FOLLOW-UP (not a card): terminalise stuck non-paper 'submitted'/'pending' rows in reconcile (list_stale_pending_paper_executions is execution_mode='paper' only); that would retire the 120s heuristic and the timestamp rule both.

cards.title: Resting (limit/GTC) exits still cannot free a stopped position — needs a broker-side OCO pair, not cancel-then-sell
cards.notes: The cancel-then-sell path (resting-stop-locks-the-position, shipped 2026-08-01) is deliberately MARKET-ONLY: a resting limit exit can sit unfilled for a session or a week, and cancelling the protective stop to place one would leave the position with no downside protection for all of that time — and the share accounting forbids holding both a full-size limit sell and a full-size stop at once, since together they commit more than is held. The correct mechanism is Alpaca's OCO order class (take-profit limit + stop-loss as ONE order, broker-arbitrated), which is exactly this shape. Measured constraint already on file: brackets/OTO work on plain GTC limits but are REFUSED on extended_hours + opg (memory alpaca-bracket-oto-measured). Deliverable: an OCO exit path behind the chokepoint so a limit exit and its stop coexist. Until then a limit exit on a stop-protected position is rejected at the chokepoint, which is the honest failure — not a silent protection downgrade.

cards.title: ✅ vix_spike auto-bought the wrong symbol on a VIX spike — symbol gate + SPY targeting
cards.notes: 2026-07-15: found while answering 'why do 4 of my 5 enabled strats never trigger?'. _vix_spike_check was purely regime-driven and NEVER read ctx.sym — on VIX>28 from calm it returned True for all 503 sp500 names, and the scan auto-bought whichever sorted first: $10k of 'A' (Agilent), entry_mode=auto, rationale 'buy-fear A long'. Its docstring claimed 'SPY-only' but strategy_scan.py:421 unconditionally skipped SPY (fetched as the market benchmark for every strategy), so it could NEVER buy its stated target. Dormant only because VIX is 16.5 — it would have misfired exactly when the market panics. FOUNDER CALL 2026-07-15: the sleeve buys SPY, the index (matches the docstring + the notional==max_deployed==$10k one-position sizing). FIX: symbol gate in _vix_spike_check (fail-closed on wrong/unset symbol); 'symbol' registered in VIX_SPIKE_ENTRY_PARAM_KEYS (load-bearing — strategy_scan.py:376 filters ctx.params to entry_param_keys, so an unregistered key is invisible to the predicate); target_symbol in strategy_scan overrides universe + bypasses the SPY benchmark-skip, honoured ONLY for kinds that register 'symbol'; seed _VIX_SPIKE_DEFAULT_PARAMS carries symbol=SPY so new installs aren't dead. 3 regression tests (all fail on main with 'assert True is False'). Reviewed by 2 parallel Opus reviewers, split mandate: static adversary found no bypass path (session_node_spy + vol_event both stay dead, triple-gated before target_symbol is computed); dynamic prover reproduced the bug through the real funnel and proved the fix end-to-end (main: ORDERS=[('auto_execute_entry','A','10000')] -> branch armed: [(...,'SPY','10000')]). Prover also proved SPY is NOT in the sp500 universe, so the skip-bypass alone was insufficient — the symbols=[target_symbol] override is what makes SPY reachable. SHIPS DISARMED: the live vix_spike row has no 'symbol' param, so post-merge it's inert (0 passed / 0 orders — safe, and strictly better than buying Agilent, but not working). FOLLOW-UPS: (1) arming = add "symbol":"SPY" to the live row + deploy; (2) FOUNDER DECISION — max_deployed_usd(10000) == notional(10000) on acct_alpaca_strat1, shared with dip_refined/earnings_drift/steepyc_dip; _open_exposure counts the WHOLE account, so vix_spike breaks its loop whenever a sibling holds anything — and VIX spikes co-occur with dips, i.e. it goes quiet exactly when it should fire. Needs a dedicated account or a raised cap. (3) pre-existing, flagged not fixed: the 'SPY only' universe option in the UI picker (strategy_universe.py:38) is still a no-op — two ways to say SPY-only, only the un-exposed one works.  —— MERGED 2026-08-01 (PR #85, opened 07-15, rebased onto a main that had moved). The strategy_scan conflict was pure adjacency — main had added the snapshot/notional block at the same spot — so both survive; the three functional hunks (target_symbol, symbols override, SPY benchmark-skip bypass) applied unchanged. ⚠️ STILL DISARMED, now twice over: the live row is enabled=0 AND carries no `symbol` param, so it scans nothing. That is deliberate — before this fix, flipping enabled=1 would have armed a $10k entry_mode=auto buy of whatever sorted first (Agilent) on the next VIX>28, on acct_alpaca_strat1. Arming is a founder decision and needs BOTH: add "symbol":"SPY" to the row and set enabled=1. Before arming, settle the sizing note below — max_deployed_usd(10000) == notional(10000) on an account shared with dip_refined/earnings_drift/steepyc_dip, and _open_exposure counts the WHOLE account, so vix_spike breaks its loop whenever a sibling holds anything, i.e. it goes quiet exactly when VIX spikes co-occur with dips.
